features.name: Accomplishments and Regard
features.text:
You have made yourself accomplished. You gain two accomplishments from the list below, and you gain more as you reach Courtier levels, as shown in the Accomplishments column of the Courtier Features table. Each accomplishment is one choice. The arts in parentheses after its name (Arms, Letters, Arts, Society, or Mysteries) are what it can count as for your Regard: when an accomplishment lists two, choose one when you take it, and it counts as that art for as long as you have it. The accomplishments are listed by the level you need to take them. Unless an accomplishment says otherwise, you can't choose the same one twice. Whenever you gain a Courtier level, you can replace one accomplishment with another for which you qualify. If you already know which college you'll join at level 3, check which art it forgoes (see Courtier Subclasses) before you choose: nothing can count as that art, and an accomplishment that lists only that art is closed to you.

**Regard.** You have presence, and you see everyone else's. Your **Regard** is the number of different arts (Arms, Letters, Arts, Society, and Mysteries) among your accomplishments. Most Courtier Colleges give up one art for good, so only a Courtier of Grace, or one who hasn't yet chosen a college, can be perfectly rounded. Some of your features grow with it.

**The Read.** When you can see and hear a group of creatures for 1 minute, or as a Study action in combat, you learn the following about a number of them up to your Regard: each one's attitude toward you; which of them has the most authority over the others, and which has the most actual power; and whether any of them is hiding hostility toward you or your companions.

**Never a Misstep.** You never commit a breach of manners by accident. In any court, house, or company, you know the forms of precedence, address, and courtesy as if you'd been raised among them, even if you've never seen their like before. You have Advantage on Charisma checks to be accepted as belonging somewhere you don't.

> **For the DM.** The Read is a reveal, and it comes whenever the Courtier asks. For any room a Courtier walks into, decide who really holds power there, and keep a line on each important creature's attitude. A Read shows *that* a creature is hiding hostility, never why, or what it means to do about it.

**From Courtier level 1**

***A Secret (Mysteries).*** You learn one spell of your choice from the Courtier spell list, of a level for which you have spell slots. It counts as a Courtier spell for you and doesn't count against the number of spells you know, and once per Long Rest you can cast it without expending a spell slot. You can take this accomplishment twice, choosing a different spell each time.

***An Instrument of Your Art (Arts).*** You gain proficiency with one musical instrument, one type of Artisan's Tools, or the Disguise Kit, and you have Advantage on ability checks you make with it. A work you make with it, given as a gift, earns you an audience with the person who receives it. You can take this accomplishment more than once, choosing a different tool each time.

***Correspondence (Letters, Society).*** You gain proficiency with Calligrapher's Supplies and the Forgery Kit. A letter you write in your own hand is opened and read by its recipient before any other mail, whoever they are, and you can tell when a letter you receive has been opened and resealed on the way, whether by a postmaster or a *cabinet noir*.

***Every Table (Society, Arts).*** You gain proficiency in two of these skills: Deception, Insight, Intimidation, or Persuasion.

***Fencing Style (Arms).*** You gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice. You can take this accomplishment twice, choosing a different feat each time.

***Horse and Bow (Arms).*** You gain proficiency with Longbows and in the Animal Handling skill, and you have Advantage on checks and saving throws to stay mounted.

***Patronage (Society, Arts).*** You have a patron at one court or great house of your choice (a king's chamber, a cardinal's household, a factor of Mutapa's House of the Bird) who will receive you, lend you modest sums, and speak for you to that court's authorities. If you lose the patron, you can find another at a different court after a month there.

***The Code (Arms, Society).*** You know the customs of the duel in any land you've lived in: who can challenge whom, over what, with which weapons, and what the law will overlook. You can serve as a second, and a challenge you carry or accept is honored by both sides. Before a fight that begins with words, you can tell whether the other side means to keep the forms.

***The Gaming House (Society, Letters).*** You gain proficiency with two Gaming Sets, and you always know when a game you're watching is crooked.

***The Hunt (Arms, Society).*** You gain proficiency in the Survival skill, and you keep a trained hawk or a brace of hounds that hunts for you but never fights. You're welcome at any hunt a court holds, and whoever rides beside you there speaks more freely than they would indoors.

***The Library (Letters).*** You gain proficiency in two of these skills: Arcana, History, Nature, or Religion.

***The Second Weapon (Arms).*** You gain proficiency with one Martial weapon of your choice, and you can use the mastery property of one kind of weapon you're proficient with (one more kind once you have Weapon Mastery).

***The Stage (Arts).*** You gain proficiency in the Performance skill and with the Disguise Kit. When you perform for at least 1 minute, you can choose one creature in the audience: until your next Long Rest, it regards you as a friend unless you give it reason not to.

***Tongues (Letters, Society).*** You learn two languages of your choice, and you can read any script used to write a language you know, however archaic. You can take this accomplishment more than once.

**From Courtier level 11**

***A Crown's Commission (Arts, Society).*** You hold an appointment as artist to one sovereign of your choice. While you serve, you have lodging at that court, a pension of 50 GP a month, and a place in its ceremonies, and your work hangs where everyone who matters will see it. Once per month you can ask the sovereign's household a favor that costs it nothing but attention: an introduction, a pass through a closed gate, a seat at a dinner.

***A Great Work (Mysteries, Arts).*** You learn one level 6 spell of your choice from any class's spell list, of any school: the masterpiece is the one time a courtier reaches past its own kind of magic. It counts as a Courtier spell for you, and you can cast it once without expending a spell slot; you regain that use when you finish a Long Rest. The masterpiece grows with you: when you reach Courtier levels 13, 15, and 17, you can replace the spell with one a level higher (level 7, then 8, then 9), and your level 9 Great Work can be *Wish* (with all of that spell's usual risks).

***A Master's Salle (Arms, Society).*** You keep a fencing school in a city of your choice, and its pupils, from younger sons to princes, owe you a student's loyalty. In that city, or at any court where one of them now serves (the DM says who's there), you can call on a pupil once a month for a sword at your side, a message carried, or a word in the right ear. A challenge issued in your school's name is always answered, and always by the person challenged.

***The Ear of the King (Society, Arms).*** Once per month, you can have a private audience of a few minutes with any ruler who has received you before, without going through their ministers. What you say reaches them exactly as you say it. What they do about it is theirs.

***The Republic of Letters (Letters, Mysteries).*** You keep a correspondence with scholars in the great cities of the world, from the Royal Society to the madrasas of Isfahan. Any library, archive, academy, or college admits you as a colleague. Once per tenday, a letter to your correspondents brings back an answer to one question of learning (history, law, languages, natural philosophy, or theology) as accurate as the learned world can make it, in the time the post takes.

features.name: Ease
features.text:
You make the hardest things look effortless, and sometimes that makes them so. You have a number of Ease points shown in the Ease column of the Courtier Features table. You regain all expended Ease when you finish a Short or Long Rest. You can spend Ease on the following options, each costing 1 Ease.

- **Make It Look Easy.** When you fail an ability check, you can spend 1 Ease to add your Charisma modifier (minimum of +1) to the roll, possibly turning it into a success.
- **With Ease.** Before you make a Charisma check, you can spend 1 Ease to treat the d20 roll as 10 plus your Regard.
- **First Through the Door.** When you roll Initiative, you can spend 1 Ease to add your Charisma modifier to the roll. If you do, you can move up to half your Speed immediately, without provoking Opportunity Attacks.
- **Not a Hair Out of Place.** When a creature you can see hits you with an attack roll while you aren't wearing Medium or Heavy armor or holding a Shield, you can take a Reaction and spend 1 Ease to add your Charisma modifier to your AC against that attack, possibly turning the hit into a miss. The DM tells you the attack's total before you decide.

You gain more options at level 2 (Ease in a Fight) and level 3 (A Light Touch, in Telling Cut).

features.name: Effortless Arms
features.text: When you make an attack roll with a weapon that has the Finesse property, you can use your Charisma modifier instead of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls.

features.name: Learned Magic
features.text:
You have learned a little magic from every tradition that would teach you. The Courtier spell list, after this class's features, gathers it: spells of presence, the mask, the read, and composure, from every class's list.

**Cantrips.** You know *Prestidigitation*, *Mending*, and *Message* (the small magic of a person who is always presentable, whose lace is never torn, and who can say a word across a crowded room), and two cantrips of your choice from the Courtier spell list. Whenever you gain a Courtier level, you can replace one of the two with another from the list.

**Spells Known.** You know two level 1 spells of your choice from the Courtier spell list. The number of spells you know increases as you gain Courtier levels, as shown in the Spells Known column of the Courtier Features table. Each spell must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

**Changing Your Spells.** Whenever you gain a Courtier level, you can replace one spell you know with another from the Courtier spell list for which you have spell slots.

**Spell Slots.** The Courtier Features table shows how many spell slots you have. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

**Spellcasting Ability.** Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your Courtier spells.

**Spellcasting Focus.** You can use any tool, musical instrument, or weapon you're proficient with as a Spellcasting Focus for your Courtier spells.

features.name: Expertise
features.text: You gain Expertise in two of your skill proficiencies of your choice. At Courtier level 9, you gain Expertise in two more.

features.name: Ease in a Fight
features.text:
Your ease reaches further into a fight. Make It Look Easy now works on saving throws as well as ability checks, and you gain this Ease option:

- **The Riposte.** When a creature you can see misses you with a melee attack, you can take a Reaction and spend 1 Ease to make one weapon attack against it.

You have one Reaction, so the choice is the art: hold it for Not a Hair Out of Place and the blow that would land, or spend it on the one that didn't.

features.name: Weapon Mastery
features.text: Your training with weapons allows you to use the mastery properties of two kinds of weapons of your choice with which you have proficiency, such as Rapiers and Shortbows. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kinds of weapons you chose.

features.name: Courtier College
features.text: You gain a Courtier College of your choice: the art that finishes you. The College of Arms, the College of Art, the College of Grace, the College of Psyche, and the College of Verse are detailed after this class's description. You gain each of your college's features at the Courtier levels shown.

features.name: Telling Cut
features.text:
Once on each of your turns when you hit a creature with a weapon attack, the creature takes extra Psychic damage equal to a roll of your Telling Cut die plus your Charisma modifier, and it can't make Opportunity Attacks against you until the start of its next turn. Your Telling Cut die is shown in the Telling Cut column of the Courtier Features table.

**A Light Touch.** When your Telling Cut lands, you can also spend 1 Ease to deal 1d8 extra damage of the weapon's type. The extra damage becomes 2d8 at Courtier level 11.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Courtier levels 8, 12, and 16.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.text: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Coming and Going
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, you can choose to be noticed or to be overlooked, for 10 minutes or until you choose again.

- *Noticed.* Every creature that can see you and isn't hostile to you stops what it's doing to watch or listen to you for as long as you hold its attention: until the effect ends, or until something more pressing (taking damage, a threat, its own urgent business) calls it away. A creature with Truesight, or that is in combat, is unaffected.
- *Overlooked.* Creatures that can see you pay you no more attention than a servant, unless you attack, cast a spell, or speak to them. You have Advantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks to go unnoticed in a crowd.

You can do this a number of times equal to your Regard, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Quick Study
features.text: If you watch a creature use a skill or a tool for at least 1 minute, or study a book or a teacher for an hour, you gain proficiency in that skill or with that tool until you finish a Long Rest. You can have only one proficiency from this feature at a time. You can't gain Expertise in a skill or tool you're proficient in only through this feature.

features.name: Witnessed
features.text: When two or more creatures make an agreement in your presence and you say aloud that you witness it, the agreement is witnessed. Each party knows when another breaks it. A creature that breaks a witnessed agreement has Disadvantage on Charisma checks against every party to it, and against you, until it makes amends, which the injured party must accept. You can have a number of witnessed agreements at once equal to your Regard.

features.name: Unshaken
features.text: You can't gain the Charmed or Frightened condition against your will. When a creature tries to Charm or Frighten you and fails, you can spend 1 Ease to turn it back: that creature must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or have the condition it tried to give you, toward you, until the end of its next turn.

features.name: Never Without Ease
features.text: When you roll Initiative and have fewer than 2 Ease points, you regain Ease until you have 2.

features.name: Epic Boon
features.text: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of the Night Spirit is recommended.

features.name: The Sun Rises
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, you can become the center of the world for 1 minute. For the duration, you regain all your Ease, and the following benefits apply:

- Your allies within 60 feet of you that can see you add your Charisma modifier to their attack rolls and saving throws.
- Hostile creatures within 60 feet of you that can see you have Disadvantage on attack rolls against any target other than you.
- Your Regard counts as 5 (6 where Reputation applies).

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

> **Playing a Courtier**
>
> You fence, you cast, and you read every room you walk into. In a fight, open with First Through the Door, fence with Charisma, and let every hit tell. Spend Ease where it matters: a failed save made good, a hit turned into a miss, a miss punished with a riposte.
>
> Try the showy thing. Make It Look Easy pays out after you fail, so the daring attempt (the leap, the bluff, the toast to the enemy's face) is the one the class covers.
>
> Choose accomplishments from different arts: your Regard, and with it your presence, grows with breadth, not depth. Out of a fight, you're the one who knows who matters in any court on earth and never puts a foot wrong in front of them.

## Courtier Spell List

| Spell Level | Presence | The Mask | The Read | Composure |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cantrip | *Friends*, *Vicious Mockery* | *Minor Illusion* | *Guidance*, *True Strike* | *Blade Ward*, *Resistance* |
| 1 | *Bless*, *Charm Person*, *Command*, *Dissonant Whispers*, *Heroism*, *Hideous Laughter*, *Sleep* | *Disguise Self*, *Illusory Script*, *Silent Image* | *Comprehend Languages*, *Detect Magic*, *Hunter's Mark*, *Identify* | *Cure Wounds*, *Healing Word*, *Protection from Evil and Good*, *Sanctuary* |
| 2 | *Calm Emotions*, *Hold Person*, *Suggestion*, *Zone of Truth* | *Invisibility*, *Magic Mouth*, *Mirror Image*, *Phantasmal Force* | *Detect Thoughts*, *Locate Object*, *See Invisibility* | *Aid*, *Arcane Lock*, *Lesser Restoration*, *Warding Bond* |
| 3 | — | *Fear*, *Major Image* | *Clairvoyance*, *Sending*, *Tongues* | *Counterspell*, *Dispel Magic*, *Glyph of Warding*, *Mass Healing Word*, *Nondetection*, *Remove Curse* |
| 4 | *Charm Monster*, *Compulsion*, *Confusion* | *Greater Invisibility*, *Hallucinatory Terrain*, *Phantasmal Killer* | *Arcane Eye*, *Divination*, *Locate Creature* | *Banishment*, *Death Ward*, *Freedom of Movement*, *Private Sanctum* |
| 5 | *Dominate Person*, *Geas*, *Hold Monster*, *Modify Memory* | *Dream*, *Mislead*, *Seeming* | *Legend Lore*, *Scrying*, *Telepathic Bond* | *Circle of Power*, *Greater Restoration* |

Every courtier also knows *Prestidigitation*, *Mending*, and *Message* (see Learned Magic): the toilette, not an art.

The columns are the schools: Presence is Enchantment, the Mask is Illusion, the Read is Divination, and Composure is Abjuration, whose *Counterspell* is the ultimate "no": the enforcement of manners made manifest. There's no *Shield* on the list: a courtier's guard is Not a Hair Out of Place. A courtier learns no fire, no summoning, no raising the dead, and no changing the shape of things: a courtier who wants to vanish takes *Invisibility*, or leaves by the door like everyone else.

subclasses.name: Arms
subclasses.lead: * The fencing schools of Madrid, Bologna, and Edo; the circle drawn on the floor of the salle; the duel at dawn and the code that governs it. Its foil is the Bard's College of Swords, from the older books: where Swords whirls, Arms is still. One cut, placed exactly. Its price: it forgoes Letters.*

features.name: The Sword or the Book
features.text:
None of your accomplishments can count as Letters, so your Regard can be no higher than 4, and an accomplishment that lists only Letters is closed to you. In exchange, you gain proficiency in the Athletics skill (if you already have it, choose another skill instead), and the master of any fencing school will open the salle to you and let you train there.

**Affairs of Honor.** You have The Code without spending an accomplishment on it (if you already have it, you gain one more accomplishment from the art of Arms instead), and people of rank bring you their quarrels: a duel you arrange is fought by its terms, and the magistrates hear of it last. Roll on the table below when someone comes to you for satisfaction.

features.name: The Challenge
features.text: As a Bonus Action, you can challenge one creature you can see within 30 feet of you. The Challenge lasts for 1 minute, and it ends early if you attack a different creature on your turn, or if you challenge someone else. The code binds both sides: while the Challenge lasts, you can use The Riposte against the challenged creature whenever it makes an attack roll against a creature other than you, as well as when it misses you. Once you reach Courtier level 5, you also have Advantage on the first attack roll you make against the creature you've challenged on each of your turns.

features.name: Economy
features.text: When you take the Attack action and could make more than one attack, you can make one attack instead. On a hit, it deals extra damage equal to a second roll of the weapon's damage dice plus your Charisma modifier, and your next use of The Riposte before the start of your next turn costs no Ease. Until you can make more than one attack (Extra Attack, at Courtier level 5), this feature waits; from then on, every turn asks the duelist's question: two cuts, or one cut and wait.

features.name: The Circle
features.text: Your Challenge draws the circle for you. While your Challenge lasts, the creature you've challenged provokes an Opportunity Attack from you when it enters your reach, and you don't provoke Opportunity Attacks from it.

features.name: Example
features.text: When the one cut from Economy hits the creature you've challenged, one ally who can see you can take a Reaction to make one weapon attack against a creature of its choice. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: One Cut
features.text: When you hit a creature with an attack, you can make the hit a Critical Hit, and the creature has Disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws until the end of its next turn. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclasses.name: Art
subclasses.lead: * Painting with light at its heart, with sculpture, architecture, and gardens around it. Its price: it forgoes Mysteries.*

features.name: What the Eye Can See
features.text: None of your accomplishments can count as Mysteries, so your Regard can be no higher than 4, and an accomplishment that lists only Mysteries is closed to you. A Great Work counts as Arts for you: your masterpiece is a painting (a different work from The Masterpiece, your level 14 feature). In exchange, you gain proficiency with Painter's Supplies and one other type of Artisan's Tools (if you already have either, choose another tool instead).

features.name: Highlight
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, you can spend 1 Ease to paint the field with light and shadow for 1 minute. Choose one creature you can see within 60 feet of you to light and one creature you can see within 60 feet of you to shadow. On each of your later turns while the painting lasts, you can move the light, the shadow, or both to other creatures you can see within 60 feet of you as a Bonus Action.

- *Lit.* The lit creature can't benefit from the Invisible condition or from being hidden, and it sheds Dim Light in a 5-foot radius. The first attack roll made against it each round adds a roll of your Telling Cut die.
- *Shadowed.* The first attack roll made against the shadowed creature each round has Disadvantage, and it can take the Hide action as a Bonus Action even if it's only in Dim Light.

features.name: The Likeness
features.text:
With 1 hour of work and Painter's Supplies, you can paint a likeness of a creature you can see. While you carry it, you have Advantage on ability checks to recognize the sitter however it's disguised and on Wisdom (Insight) checks against it; you know if the sitter dies, and roughly how (the paint darkens, cracks, or runs); and the likeness counts as a likeness for spells such as *Scrying*, but no one can scry the sitter through it unless you allow it. You can carry a number of likenesses equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of 1).

**Commissions.** Your work hangs in great houses, and a garden, a ceiling, or a portrait you made is a door into any house that owns it: its household will receive you as a guest. Roll on the commission table below when you're between jobs.

features.name: Trompe-l'oeil
features.text:
When you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with a painting: spend 1 Ease and choose one:

- *A Painted Wall.* A wall up to 15 feet long, 10 feet high, and 1 inch thick appears in unoccupied spaces within 60 feet of you until the start of your next turn. It blocks movement and line of sight, and attacks can't pass through it.
- *A Painted Door.* You paint a door on a wall, floor, or ceiling no more than 5 feet thick within 30 feet of you. Until the start of your next turn, any creature can pass through it as if it were open. A creature inside the wall when the door closes is shunted to the nearer side.

**Anamorphosis.** When you write, draw, or paint something, you can make it legible only to creatures you choose; anyone else sees a smear, a landscape, or a different picture of your choice. *Detect Magic* shows it as magical, but only *True Seeing* or your permission reads it.

features.name: Perspective
features.text: As a Bonus Action, you can spend 1 Ease to choose a point you can see within 60 feet of you. Until the start of your next turn, the space within 30 feet of that point is drawn to it: each creature of your choice moving toward the point moves 10 extra feet when it moves, and every other creature in that space treats it as Difficult Terrain when it moves away from the point.

features.name: The Masterpiece
features.text: You make the one great work of your career: a painting, a ceiling, a garden, or a building, made over at least a month of downtime. While it stands, the house that holds it can't be perceived through divination magic unless you allow it, and you always know the direction and distance to it. Anyone who has stood before it and been moved by it treats you as a friend the first time you meet.

subclasses.name: Grace
subclasses.lead: * Montaigne's essays, Gracián's art of worldly wisdom, the salon, the tea ceremony: life itself as the art worth mastering. Not the College of Dance: no footwork, no unarmed strikes. A Bard performs; Grace is the performance, and it never steps off the stage. Its price: none. Grace is the balanced center and forgoes no art, so only a Courtier of Grace can reach a Regard of 5.*

features.name: Conversation
features.text:
When you spend at least 1 minute in conversation with a creature that can understand you, outside combat, you can spend 1 Ease to change its attitude toward you by one step (from hostile to indifferent, or from indifferent to friendly) without a check. It doesn't realize anything has been done to it. You can't use this feature on the same creature again until you finish a Long Rest.

**The Hostess.** You can use With Ease on a Charisma check made by an ally who can see or hear you, spending your own Ease. You set up the bard's plea or the soldier's clumsy toast, and it lands.

features.name: Composure
features.text: While you aren't Frightened, you and your allies within 10 feet of you have Advantage on saving throws to avoid or end the Frightened condition. In addition, when an ally you can see within 30 feet of you fails a saving throw, you can use Make It Look Easy on its roll as if it were yours.

features.name: Poise Under Fire
features.text:
When an ally you can see within 30 feet of you gains the Charmed, Frightened, or Stunned condition, you can take a Reaction and spend 1 Ease to end that condition on it.

**A Word in Time.** You can use Not a Hair Out of Place when an ally you can see within 10 feet of you is hit by an attack roll, adding your Charisma modifier to the ally's AC against that attack instead of to yours. Your composure is catching: a hand on the arm, a word at the right moment, and the blow goes wide.

features.name: Reputation
features.text: In any settlement where you've spent at least a week, people of every rank know who you are, and your Regard counts as 1 higher there, even above 5 (so you Read one more creature, With Ease counts one higher, and so on). You're offered lodging in a good house without asking, invitations find you within a day of your arrival, and any host who receives you is honored to have done so.

features.name: The Life Is the Work
features.text: When you or an ally you can see within 60 feet of you would fail a D20 Test, you can make it a success instead. Whatever happened becomes a story people tell, at court and in taverns, and it's always told in your favor. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclasses.name: Psyche
subclasses.lead: * Music stays the Bard's, so Psyche works the passions themselves: Le Brun's lecture on the expression of the passions (1668) and Descartes's* Passions of the Soul *(1649). Its price: it forgoes Arts.*

features.name: People, Not Canvases
features.text: None of your accomplishments can count as Arts, so your Regard can be no higher than 4, and an accomplishment that lists only Arts is closed to you. In exchange, you gain proficiency in the Insight and Medicine skills (if you already have either, choose another skill instead), and the physicians of any hospital will let you work beside them.

features.name: Wanting and Fearing
features.text:
When you see a creature's face, you know which passion is strongest in it: fear, desire, grief, rage, or joy. As a Bonus Action, you can work on one creature you can see within 60 feet of you:

- *Stir.* A hostile creature's passion rises: it has Disadvantage on the next attack roll or saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn. Stirring costs 1 Ease, or nothing if the creature has made an attack roll against you since the end of your last turn.
- *Settle.* For 1 Ease, a creature's passion subsides: it has Advantage on the next saving throw it makes before the start of your next turn, and if it has the Charmed or Frightened condition, that condition ends.

Stir spoils one roll for a foe, and anyone who has come at you is already halfway there; Settle steadies one roll for a friend.

features.name: Boundless Passion
features.text: When you Settle a creature, each other creature of your choice within 10 feet of it also gains Settle's benefit. When a creature you've Stirred makes an attack roll against you before the start of your next turn, it takes Psychic damage equal to a roll of your Telling Cut die, whether it hits or misses.

features.name: Catharsis
features.text: When you Settle a creature, or end a condition on a creature with a spell, it regains Hit Points equal to a roll of your Telling Cut die plus your Charisma modifier. (The creatures that Boundless Passion spreads Settle to don't regain Hit Points.)

features.name: Mastery of the Passions
features.text: You can work on a whole crowd's passions at once. Outside combat, you can spend 10 minutes among a crowd, a household, or a gathering of up to a few hundred people and choose one passion to Stir or Settle in all of them: a riot cools, a feud's two families can sit at one table for the evening, a frightened town takes heart, or a festive one turns ugly. The crowd doesn't know it was you. The effect lasts until the next dawn, and you can't use this feature again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclasses.name: Verse
subclasses.lead: * Shakespeare's heirs, Molière, the commedia, kabuki, the ghazal, the pulpit orator, the filí's satire. Its price: it forgoes Arms.*

features.name: The Stage over the Field
features.text:
None of your accomplishments can count as Arms, so your Regard can be no higher than 4, and an accomplishment that lists only Arms is closed to you. In exchange, you gain proficiency in the Performance skill and with the Disguise Kit (if you already have either, choose another skill or tool instead), and you can perform anything you've seen performed, even once. You also gain a Fighting Style feat of your choice: stage swordplay is choreography, but it's choreography with a real blade.

**The Repertory.** A company or a patron will take you on for a season wherever plays are licensed, and some will hide you where they aren't. Roll on the table below when you're between engagements.

features.name: The Mask
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, you can spend 1 Ease to put on a mask and become an archetype for 1 minute. Until that minute ends, you can change to another mask as a Bonus Action without spending Ease, or take yours off (no action required). You can wear one mask at a time.

- **The Captain** swaggers. The first time on each of your turns that you hit a creature with a weapon, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or have Disadvantage on attack rolls against you until the end of its next turn.
- **Harlequin** tumbles. Your Speed increases by 10 feet, you can take the Dash or Disengage action as a Bonus Action, and climbing and jumping cost you no extra movement.
- **The Pedant** is always certain. You have Advantage on Intelligence checks, and on Wisdom (Insight) checks to tell whether a creature is lying.
- **Pantaloon** bargains. The first time on each of its turns that a creature that can hear you would attack you, it must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC or offer you terms instead and lose that attack: it can't make the attack against you or anyone else, whether or not you accept its terms. The DM says what it thinks is a fair bargain.
- **Columbine** sees through everyone. Once on each of your turns (no action required), you can look closely at one creature or object you can see within 30 feet of you: you see through any illusion, disguise, or shape-change on it, and you know a shape-changer for what it is. This isn't Truesight: it doesn't show you what's invisible or what's on another plane.

At courts where the commedia isn't played, other companies' stock roles stand in: kabuki's hero, villain, and lover; the jingju opera's painted faces.

features.name: The Aside
features.text:
You can speak to one creature you can see within 60 feet of you so that no one else hears you, even in a crowd or a fight. When you do, you can make your words land as if you'd had an hour with it: if it can understand you, you make one Charisma check against it with Advantage, and its attitude toward you can't worsen because of what you said. Once you make your words land this way, you can't do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

**The Cutting Line.** You know *Vicious Mockery*; if you already did, learn another cantrip from the Courtier spell list. When you take the Attack action, you can replace one of your attacks with a casting of *Vicious Mockery*, and Telling Cut applies to it when the target fails its save, as if you'd hit it with a weapon. The poet stabs once and insults once, and the insult is the better choice against a foe whose armor is thick and whose wits are thin.

features.name: Satire
features.text: As a Bonus Action, you can spend 1 Ease to mock a creature you can see within 60 feet of you that can hear you. It takes Psychic damage equal to two rolls of your Telling Cut die plus your Charisma modifier, and it has Disadvantage on its next saving throw before the end of your next turn while everyone who heard you laughs.

features.name: All the World
features.text:
Your work is known: any company of players anywhere in the world will stage a play of yours, and any court that keeps a stage will receive you as its author.

You've played every part, and now you can play two at once: you can wear two masks at the same time.

multiclass.gains: Hit Point Die, proficiency in one skill of your choice, and training with Light armor
multiclass.text: You must have a Charisma score of 13 or higher. Gain the following traits from the Core Courtier Traits table: Hit Point Die, proficiency in one skill of your choice, and training with Light armor. Gain the Courtier's level 1 features, which are listed in the Courtier Features table. For multiclass spell slots, add half your Courtier levels (round up). If you have more levels in another class than in this one, your Ease maximum can't exceed your Courtier level, you regain expended Ease only when you finish a Long Rest, and Telling Cut adds your Regard instead of your Charisma modifier.

data.name: Mhizha
data.blurb: Int half caster. Mutapa’s artificer: magic through tools, and an Arc Gun in the fight.

traits.value: *Choose 2:* Arcana, History, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, Perception, or Sleight of Hand
Simple weapons, and Martial weapons that have the Ammunition and Loading properties
Tinker's Tools, and one type of Artisan's Tools of your choice
Light and Medium armor and Shields
*Choose A or B:* (A) Scale Mail, Shield, Dagger, Tinker's Tools, the Artisan's Tools you chose, Dungeoneer's Pack, and 10 GP; or (B) 150 GP

features.name: Spellcasting
features.text:
You cast spells through the tools in your hands. See the rules on spellcasting for how spells work. The information below details how you use those rules with Mhizha spells, which appear in the Mhizha spell list later in the class's description.

**Cantrips.** You know two cantrips of your choice from the Mhizha spell list. *Guidance* and *Prestidigitation* are recommended. Whenever you gain a Mhizha level, you can replace one of your cantrips with another cantrip of your choice from the Mhizha spell list. When you reach Mhizha levels 10 and 14, you learn another cantrip of your choice from the Mhizha spell list, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Mhizha Features table.

**Spell Slots.** The Mhizha Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

**Prepared Spells of Level 1+.** You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Mhizha spells. *Cure Wounds* and *Faerie Fire* are recommended. The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Mhizha levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Mhizha Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Mhizha spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots. If another Mhizha feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Mhizha spells for you.

**Changing Your Prepared Spells.** When you finish a Long Rest, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells there with other Mhizha spells for which you have spell slots.

**Spellcasting Ability.** Intelligence is your spellcasting ability for your Mhizha spells.

**Spellcasting Focus.** You cast Mhizha spells through a tool: Tinker's Tools, Artisan's Tools you're proficient with, or your Arc Gun. You must be holding one of them to cast a Mhizha spell, even one with no Material component, and it serves as your Spellcasting Focus for that spell; the hand holding it can perform the spell's Somatic components.

features.name: Arc Gun
features.text:
You carry a weapon of your own design that throws lightning. The Arc Gun is a magic item that only you can fire.

**Firing It.** The coil holds one charge and a shot spends all of it, so firing the Arc Gun is the whole of your Attack action: make a ranged attack roll using Intelligence against a creature or object within 120 feet of yourself, adding your Proficiency Bonus. On a hit, the target takes Lightning damage equal to the dice shown in the Arc Gun column of the Mhizha Features table plus your Intelligence modifier. You can fire the Arc Gun only once per turn. This is a ranged attack, not a weapon or spell attack. You must hold the Arc Gun to fire it, and it takes one hand, so you can fire it with a Shield on your other arm; you can draw or stow it as part of the attack, as with a weapon.

**Rebuilding It.** If the Arc Gun is lost (out of your possession for 1 hour) or destroyed, you can build a new one with Tinker's Tools over the course of a Long Rest; the old one stops working.

features.name: Tinker
features.text:
With Tinker's Tools and 1 minute of work, you can mend a single break or tear in a nonmagical object you touch, as the *Mending* cantrip does, or build a Tiny clockwork trinket that does one simple thing (ticks, chimes at a set hour, walks in a line, plays a few bars of music). A trinket stops working after 8 hours. You can have a number of trinkets equal to your Proficiency Bonus at a time; if you build another, your oldest stops working.

*Arc Lamp.* A trinket can be an Arc Lamp *(Electrical)*. It sheds Bright Light in a 30-foot radius and Dim Light for an additional 30 feet, or in a 60-foot Cone and Dim Light for an additional 60 feet. It has no flame, works underwater, and can be shuttered or opened as a Bonus Action.

*Retuning.* You can hear when a device has drifted. With Tinker's Tools and 10 minutes of work, you can retune a Mutapan curiosity (a self-lighting lamp, a stove, a pump, any small work that has fallen out of calibration) so it works as new. Anyone a Mhizha has taught can do the same in an hour; no one else can do it at all. Abroad, this pays: the owner of a drifting lamp is usually rich, often grateful, and sometimes talkative, and a retuning can get you through a door that a letter of introduction wouldn't. A retuning's going rate, and whether Mutapa's merchant houses mind a Mhizha doing it for free.

features.name: Preparations
features.text:
You make your own smoke, slick, and flash. When you finish a Long Rest, you can spend 1 hour of it with Tinker's Tools to make a number of Preparations equal to your Proficiency Bonus; from level 2, it's the same hour in which you build your devices. They last until you finish your next Long Rest, and only you know how to use them. Preparations aren't magical.

As a Bonus Action, you expend a Preparation and throw it at a point you can see within 30 feet of yourself, and choose which kind it is. Its saving throw uses your spell save DC.

- *Smoke.* A 10-foot-radius Sphere centered on that point is Heavily Obscured until the end of your next turn. A strong wind disperses it.
- *Slick.* A 10-foot square centered on that point is Difficult Terrain for 1 minute. Each creature in the square when it appears, and each creature that enters it or starts its turn there, makes a Dexterity saving throw; on a failed save, it has the Prone condition. (A Prone creature is easy for your friends' blades and hard to hit from range, your Arc Gun included.)
- *Flash.* Each creature in a 5-foot-radius Sphere centered on that point makes a Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it has the Blinded condition until the end of its next turn.

features.name: Devices
features.text:
You build small devices that each do one thing well. You know every design under Device Designs, below, for which you qualify.

**Building Devices.** When you finish a Long Rest, you can spend 1 hour of it with Tinker's Tools to build devices, each of a different design. The number you build is shown in the Devices column of the Mhizha Features table. In the same hour, you make your Preparations (see above). When you build devices, any you built earlier stop working. You can use a device yourself or hand it to another creature; a device works for whoever wears or holds it.

*Reading the Job.* Build for what's coming. A Mhizha who hears tonight that the vault is under the canal builds the Breathing Helm and the Lockbreaker before morning, and the DM's hints about tomorrow are worth listening for.

**Magical and Electrical.** A device marked *Electrical* isn't magic: it runs on the current it has stored, enough to work where magic fails, so an Antimagic Field or *Dispel Magic* doesn't stop it. Every other device is a magic item that doesn't require Attunement; it stops working in an Antimagic Field or if you die.

**Durability and Loss.** A device is an object with AC 15 and 5 Hit Points; at 0 Hit Points it is destroyed. A device is lost if it has been out of your possession, and out of the possession of anyone you gave it to, for 1 hour.

#### Device Designs

**Charged Plate** *(Electrical)*. The plate isn't armor, and it can be worn with armor. When the wearer finishes a Short or Long Rest, the wearer gains Temporary Hit Points equal to your Mhizha level plus your Intelligence modifier.

**Clockwork Servant.** A Tiny clockwork figure that works as the servant created by the *Unseen Servant* spell, except that it's visible, it obeys a creature you designate when you build it, and it lasts until you build the device again.

**Lockbreaker** *(Electrical)*. A creature using it with Thieves' Tools adds your Intelligence modifier to checks to pick locks and disarm traps.

**Shock Gauntlet** *(Electrical)*. Once on each of its turns, when the wearer hits a creature with an Unarmed Strike or an attack with a melee weapon, the creature takes an extra 1d4 Lightning damage.

**Spring Boots.** The wearer's jump distances are tripled, and it takes no damage from a fall of 30 feet or less.

**Grapple Line** *(Electrical; Prerequisite: Mhizha level 5)*. Once on each of its turns, as a Bonus Action, the holder can fire the line at a solid surface within 60 feet of itself and be pulled in a straight line to an unoccupied space next to that point. This movement doesn't cost the holder any Speed, and it provokes Opportunity Attacks as normal.

**Night Lenses** *(Prerequisite: Mhizha level 5)*. The wearer has Darkvision with a range of 60 feet.

**Seeing Spectacles** *(Prerequisite: Mhizha level 5)*. The wearer sees creatures and objects that have the Invisible condition within 30 feet of itself as if they were visible, and has Advantage on Intelligence (Investigation) checks to discern an illusion.

**Breathing Helm** *(Prerequisite: Mhizha level 9)*. The wearer can breathe underwater and isn't affected by smoke or by gas that must be inhaled, and it sees clearly underwater. It doesn't let the wearer see through an area that is Heavily Obscured.

**Speaking Wires** *(Electrical; Prerequisite: Mhizha level 9)*. Two handsets joined by nothing anyone can see. Whoever holds one can speak in a whisper to whoever holds the other, if the two are within 1 mile of each other.

**Flight Pack** *(Prerequisite: Mhizha level 13)*. The wearer has a Fly Speed equal to its Speed. The wearer turns the pack on or off (no action required). The pack works for a total of 1 hour, in increments of 1 minute or more, and then not again until you build it again.

features.name: Mhizha Subclass
features.text: You gain a Mhizha subclass of your choice: the Chemist, the Constructor, the Gunner, the Lionskin, or the Mapmaker. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Mhizha levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Mhizha level or lower.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Mhizha levels 8, 12, and 16.

features.name: Overcharge
features.text: Once per turn, when you hit a creature with the Arc Gun, you can expend a spell slot to overcharge the shot. The creature takes an extra 2d8 Lightning damage, plus 1d8 for each spell slot level above 1.

features.name: Field Workshop
features.text: You keep a workshop in your pack. When you finish a Short Rest, you regain two expended Preparations (three from level 13), and with Tinker's Tools you can rebuild one device that was lost or destroyed since your last Long Rest, unless you destroyed it or gave it up on purpose.

features.name: Flare
features.text: When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you makes an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to expend a Preparation and throw it as a Flash at the attacker before the roll; only the attacker is affected. It makes a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, it has the Blinded condition until the end of its next turn, including against the triggering attack.

features.name: How It Works
features.text: You can spend 1 minute handling an object to learn what it does. If it's a magic item, you learn its properties as if you had cast *Identify* on it. If it's a mechanism, a lock, or a trap, you learn how it works, and you have Advantage on ability checks to operate, open, or disarm it.

features.name: Arc Chain
features.text: When you hit a creature with the Arc Gun, lightning leaps from it to a second creature you can see within 10 feet of it, which takes damage of the shot's type equal to your Intelligence modifier.

features.name: Master Artisan
features.text: Choose two of your tool proficiencies. You have Expertise with them. In addition, crafting a magic item takes you two-thirds as long and costs two-thirds as much as normal.

features.name: Overload
features.text: When you overcharge a shot, the creature Arc Chain leaps to also takes the Overcharge's extra damage.

features.name: The Sealed Art
features.text:
You can set glamour in platinum (*The Setting*, Characters, Wonders and Curiosities, The Hidden as Material). In addition:

- **Living Devices.** When you build devices, you can set one platinum measure into one of them. While the device is worn or held, its holder can release the measure's property as a Bonus Action instead of a Magic action. It recharges at dawn, as any platinum measure does.
- **The Arc Remembers.** You can set one platinum measure into your Arc Gun. When you overcharge a shot, you can also release that property on the target as part of the hit, using your spell save DC in place of DC 13. A property that fills an area or reaches the creatures around you (Mist, Light, Song, Frost) is centered on the target, and Thorn affects the target as if you had touched it. A property that moves you or works on an object (Step, Seeming, Return) works as it normally does and doesn't affect the target.
- **A Door of Your Own.** Once per Long Rest, as a Magic action, you can open a door into the Hidden on any surface. It stays open for 1 minute and leads to a pocket that only you and creatures you choose can find again: a sealed room, 30 feet on a side, that keeps whatever you leave in it.

features.name: Grounded
features.text: You have Resistance to Lightning and Thunder damage, and Advantage on Constitution saving throws to maintain Concentration.

features.name: Epic Boon
features.text: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Fate is recommended.

features.name: Lightning Itself
features.text:
The Arc Gun's damage (the shot's, including extra damage your features add to the shot) ignores Resistance, and a creature with Immunity to the shot's damage type has Resistance to it instead. Its damage rises to 5d10, as shown in the Arc Gun column of the Mhizha Features table.

> **Playing a Mhizha**
>
> You're the party's workshop. Each morning you build the day's devices and hand most of them out: the Shock Gauntlet and the Charged Plate to whoever stands in front, Spring Boots or the Grapple Line to whoever has to get up the wall. When you know tonight what tomorrow's job is, build for it.
>
> In a fight, fire the Arc Gun every turn and spend your Bonus Action on a Preparation: Smoke to cover a retreat, Flash on the most dangerous enemy, Slick to drop a crowd for your friends' blades (not for your Arc Gun, since a Prone target is hard to hit from range). From 5th level, Overcharge turns a spell slot into a heavy hit; from 7th, Flare can blind an attacker before its roll.
>
> Keep a tool in your hand: every Mhizha spell is cast through one. Out of a fight, your hands open doors. You mend, you take things apart to see how they work, and abroad a drifting Mutapan lamp gets you into houses a letter of introduction wouldn't.

## Mhizha Spell List

#### Cantrips (Level 0 Mhizha Spells)

Dancing Lights, Guidance, Light, Mage Hand, Mending, Message, Prestidigitation, Resistance, Spare the Dying

#### Level 1 Mhizha Spells

Alarm, Cure Wounds, Detect Magic, Disguise Self, Expeditious Retreat, Faerie Fire, False Life, Feather Fall, Floating Disk, Identify, Jump, Longstrider, Purify Food and Drink, Sanctuary, Thunderwave, Unseen Servant

#### Level 2 Mhizha Spells

Acid Arrow, Aid, Alter Self, Arcane Lock, Blur, Continual Flame, Darkvision, Enhance Ability, Enlarge/Reduce, Heat Metal, Invisibility, Knock, Lesser Restoration, Levitate, Locate Object, Magic Mouth, Magic Weapon, Rope Trick, See Invisibility, Spider Climb, Web

#### Level 3 Mhizha Spells

Blink, Dispel Magic, Fly, Gaseous Form, Glyph of Warding, Haste, Lightning Bolt, Protection from Energy, Revivify, Tiny Hut, Water Breathing, Water Walk

#### Level 4 Mhizha Spells

Arcane Eye, Fabricate, Faithful Hound, Fire Shield, Freedom of Movement, Resilient Sphere, Secret Chest, Stone Shape, Stoneskin

#### Level 5 Mhizha Spells

Animate Objects, Arcane Hand, Creation, Greater Restoration, Passwall, Telekinesis, Wall of Stone

features.name: Tria Prima
features.text:
You gain proficiency with Alchemist's Supplies; if you already have it, choose another type of Artisan's Tools. When you build your devices, you can also use Alchemist's Supplies to make a batch of three elixirs (four from level 10), each of a kind you choose as you make it, in any mix: Salt, Sulfur, or Mercury. An elixir is magical, and it lasts until you finish your next Long Rest. A creature can drink an elixir, or administer it to a creature within 5 feet of itself, as a Bonus Action.

- *Salt* (the body). The drinker regains Hit Points equal to 2d8 plus your Intelligence modifier.
- *Sulfur* (the soul). For 1 minute, once on each of the drinker's turns when it hits a creature with an attack roll, that creature takes an extra 1d6 Fire damage.
- *Mercury* (the spirit). For 1 minute, the drinker's Speed increases by 10 feet, and Opportunity Attacks against it have Disadvantage.

*Assay.* With Alchemist's Supplies and 10 minutes of work, you learn what a sample of metal, ore, or coin is made of and how pure it is: whether gold is good, whether silver has been cut, and whether a bar has been weighted with a gray metal that isn't silver. Merchants, mints, and moneylenders pay well for this, and a House of the Bird assayer's word is accepted from Sofala to Surat. Whether the bank licenses assayers, and what it costs to be one.

features.name: Nigredo
features.text:
You begin the Work by breaking matter down. When you fire the Arc Gun, you can have it deal Acid damage instead of Lightning damage; Lightning Itself applies to the shot whatever its damage type. When Arc Chain would leap from an Acid shot, you can instead have the acid keep working: the target takes Acid damage equal to your Intelligence modifier at the start of its next turn.

*Vitriol.* You can throw a Preparation as Vitriol, a fourth kind. Each creature in a 5-foot-radius Sphere centered on that point makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a failed save, it takes Acid damage equal to your Intelligence modifier and has a −2 penalty to Armor Class until the end of your next turn.

In addition, with Alchemist's Supplies and 10 minutes of work, you can dissolve a nonmagical object that fits in a 1-foot Cube and isn't being worn or carried (a lock, a hinge, a length of chain) into a black residue.

features.name: Albedo
features.text:
You purify what you have broken down. Your Salt elixir also ends the Poisoned condition and one disease on the drinker. You have Resistance to Poison damage, and you can purify food and drink you touch as the *Purify Food and Drink* spell does (no action required).

*Green Salt.* You know how to make the field dressing Mutapa's farms run on. During downtime, with Alchemist's Supplies, a week of work, and materials worth 50 GP, you can dress a farm's fields so that its next harvest is a good one, whatever else the season does short of drought, flood, or locusts. What that's worth to the farm's owner is for the DM; in a lean year, a great deal, and a village that's eaten through a famine on your dressing remembers you. Where Mutapa's nitrogen comes from: platinum makes the acid, but making the ammonia takes an iron catalyst.

features.name: Citrinitas
features.text:
The Work wakes. Your Salt elixir restores 3d8 Hit Points plus your Intelligence modifier, and each batch of elixirs you make has four elixirs. In addition, when you make your elixirs, you can combine any two of them into a single draught (which uses up both), and it grants both effects when it's drunk.

*A Drop on the Tongue.* You can identify a potion, poison, or drug by tasting a drop of it over 1 minute. You learn what it is and what it does, and you suffer none of its effects from the taste.

features.name: Rubedo
features.text: You complete the Work. When you finish a Long Rest, you can also make the Stone, a red tincture that lasts until you finish your next Long Rest. A creature that drinks the Stone (a Bonus Action) is protected for 8 hours: the first time it would drop to 0 Hit Points without dying outright, it drops to 1 Hit Point instead, and the protection ends.

features.name: Construct
features.text:
You build a companion. It uses the Construct stat block below and is friendly to you and your allies. It shares your Initiative and takes its turn immediately after yours. It can move and use its Reaction on its own. On its turn, it makes its Strike if you took the Attack action on your turn; otherwise it takes the Dodge action, unless you took a Bonus Action to command it to take the Dash, Disengage, Help, or Utilize action. If you have the Incapacitated condition, it can take any action of its choice.

If it drops to 0 Hit Points, it stops working, but it isn't destroyed. When you finish a Long Rest, it starts working again if it had stopped, and it regains all its Hit Points. If your construct is destroyed (its works smashed, melted, or disintegrated) or lost, you can build a new one with Tinker's Tools over the course of a Long Rest. It's built light, to take the first blows meant for you: at low levels, expect it to stop in the day's first hard fight and wait for morning (from level 6, Restart brings it back once).

**Construct**

- *Medium Construct, Neutral.* AC 15. Hit Points 2 plus your Intelligence modifier plus twice your Mhizha level. Speed 40 ft.
- *Abilities.* Str 14, Dex 12, Con 14, Int 4, Wis 10, Cha 4.
- *Saving Throws and Checks.* Its ability modifiers plus your Proficiency Bonus.
- *Immunities.* Poison; the Poisoned condition. Darkvision 60 ft. It understands the languages you know but can't speak.
- *In the Doorway.* Enemies can't move through the construct's space. A creature the construct hits with an Opportunity Attack has a Speed of 0 until the end of the current turn.
- *Strike.* Melee Attack Roll: Bonus equals your spell attack modifier, reach 5 ft. Hit: Force damage equal to 1d8 plus your Intelligence modifier.

*Hands for Hire.* Out of a fight, your construct can work a simple, repetitive task (hauling, digging, pumping, turning a mill, carrying one end of a litter) for up to 8 hours without supervision or rest, doing the work of two strong laborers.

features.name: Field Repairs
features.text:
When you finish a Short Rest, your construct regains Hit Points equal to half its Hit Point maximum if it's still working.

*Restart.* As a Magic action with Tinker's Tools, you can restart your stopped construct within 5 feet of you, under fire or after the fight; it starts working again with Hit Points equal to half your Mhizha level (round down). Once you restart it, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

*Loaded.* You can throw a Preparation, or use Flare, as if you were standing in your construct's space.

*Sentry.* Your construct doesn't sleep. While you rest, it can keep watch; if it sees or hears a creature it doesn't know within 60 feet of itself, it wakes you with a chime only you can hear.

features.name: Improved Construct
features.text:
Your construct's Strike deals 2d8 Force damage plus your Intelligence modifier.

*Errand.* You can send your construct on an errand to a place or person within 1 mile of you that you describe to it: to carry an object or a sealed message there, wait for an answer if you tell it to, and come back. It takes the route you'd take. It can't speak, and anyone who's met a Constructor knows to put the answer in writing.

features.name: Fail-Safe
features.text: Once per Long Rest, when your construct drops to 0 Hit Points, it drops to half its Hit Point maximum instead.

features.name: Turret
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, you set down a turret in an unoccupied space you can see within 10 feet of yourself. It is a Small object with AC 15, Hit Points equal to twice your Mhizha level, and Immunity to Poison and Psychic damage. It lasts for 1 hour, until it drops to 0 Hit Points, or until you set down another. You can set down a turret twice, and you regain both uses when you finish a Long Rest.

While your turret is deployed, it fires whenever you take the Attack action, once per turn (no action required): make a ranged spell attack against a creature the turret can see within 60 feet of it. The turret doesn't fire while you're more than 120 feet away from it. On a hit, the target takes Force damage equal to 1d6 plus your Intelligence modifier.

*Mobile Turret.* As a Bonus Action while you're within 5 feet of your turret, you can pick it up and set it down again in an unoccupied space within 10 feet of yourself. This doesn't use one of your turrets.

*Rangefinder.* You know the distance to anything you can see, out to a mile, and the height of anything you can see the top and bottom of, to within a few feet. With 10 minutes and Tinker's Tools you can also tell whether ground is level, which way water will run on it, and whether a wall, bridge, or roof is sound.

features.name: Forward Observer
features.text:
While you're within 120 feet of your turret, you can see and hear through it as well as through your own eyes and ears (no action required), and you can fire the Arc Gun or throw a Preparation as if you were standing in the turret's space.

*Watch.* When you set down your turret out of a fight, you can set it to watch instead of fire. While it watches, it doesn't attack and lasts for 8 hours instead of 1, but if a creature you didn't designate when you set it down comes within 60 feet of it, it sounds a chime that you hear if you're within 1 mile of it.

features.name: Shells
features.text:
When you would fire the Arc Gun, you can fire a shell instead. Each creature in a 10-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point you can see within 120 feet of yourself makes a Dexterity saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes Force damage equal to the Arc Gun's dice plus your Intelligence modifier; on a successful save, it takes half as much damage. Firing a shell is your Attack action, so your turret fires too. You can fire two shells, and you regain both when you finish a Long Rest.

*Signal Shell.* Out of a fight, you can fire a shell that does no damage and isn't expended: it bursts as a light and a sound seen and heard for miles, in a color and pattern you choose. Fired in a code you've agreed in advance, it carries a short message.

features.name: Bulwark
features.text:
While within 10 feet of your turret, you and your allies have a +2 bonus to Armor Class against ranged attack rolls.

*Siegecraft.* With 1 hour to study a fortification, you learn its weakest point, roughly how long it would hold against an assault or a siege, and what it would take to make it hold longer. You have Advantage on any ability check to plan, build, or break a fortification.

features.name: Powered Suit
features.text:
If you have training with Medium armor, you gain Heavy armor training (a multiclass Mhizha with only Light armor training gains none, and wears the suit untrained). With Tinker's Tools and 1 hour of work, you can make any armor you wear into your suit. Whatever it was made from, the suit is Heavy armor with a base Armor Class of 18 (your Dexterity doesn't add to it), it has no Strength requirement for you, and you have Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks while you wear it. You can have only one suit at a time; if you make another, the old one is ordinary armor again. The suit's systems run down both arms, so while you hold a Shield, you can't benefit from the suit's Armor Class, and it gives none of the following benefits. While you wear it, the following benefits apply:

- *Built In.* The Arc Gun is built into the suit; you fire it without holding it, and the suit is your Spellcasting Focus, so you don't need to hold a tool to cast a Mhizha spell.
- *Gauntlets.* You can deliver the Arc Gun's shot as a blow: firing it at a creature within 5 feet of you doesn't give you Disadvantage, and you can have that shot deal Force damage instead of Lightning damage. Your Unarmed Strikes deal Force damage equal to 1 plus your Intelligence modifier, and you use Intelligence for their attack rolls.
- *Tailored.* A suit is cut to pass. Out of a fight, it can look like ordinary clothes of your station: court dress, a merchant's coat, a laborer's wrap. A creature that looks closely can tell it's armor with a successful Wisdom (Perception) check against your spell save DC.
- *Model.* When you finish a Long Rest, choose the suit's model. *Infiltrator:* the suit doesn't give you Disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks, and your Speed increases by 10 feet. *Guardian:* the suit is built for the gate: you gain a +1 bonus to Armor Class while you wear it. In addition, when a creature you can see hits an ally within 5 feet of you with an attack roll, you can take a Reaction to reduce the damage by 1d10 plus your Intelligence modifier; you can do this a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Kinetic Charge
features.text: The suit drinks the force that strikes it. When you take damage while you wear it (damage to Temporary Hit Points counts), or you reduce damage with the Guardian's Reaction, the suit becomes charged; it holds one charge at a time. An Infiltrator suit also becomes charged when you roll Initiative. The charge is the suit's whole store, and it goes out in one blow: when you hit a creature with the Arc Gun while the suit is charged, you can release the charge. The creature takes an extra 1d6 Force damage (2d6 if the suit is an Infiltrator). This extra damage increases by 1d6 when you reach Mhizha level 5. The charge fades if you take off the suit or finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Suit Systems
features.text:
You gain the following benefits:

- *Built-In Curiosity.* When you build devices, you can also build one Mutapan curiosity into the suit, and change it whenever you build devices again: a curiosity from the Mutapan Curiosities table (*The Setting*, Characters, Wonders and Curiosities), or another small convenience the DM allows, such as a lamp in the faceplate that lights on a word; a gauntlet stove that boils water in a minute; a pump in the boots that clears a flooded room or a holed boat; or a speaking-horn that carries your voice to anyone within 300 feet. It works only for you while you wear the suit, and it's lost or destroyed only if the suit is.
- *Model Systems.* *Infiltrator:* you have a Climb Speed equal to your Speed, and when you fall, you take no damage and can move horizontally up to twice the distance you fall. *Guardian:* when you use the Guardian's Reaction to protect an ally within 5 feet of you, you can swap places with it, as long as you're both willing.

features.name: Improved Models
features.text:
*Infiltrator:* as a Bonus Action, you can release the suit's charge to have the Invisible condition until the start of your next turn. *Guardian:* you can't be moved against your will or given the Prone condition while you wear the suit, and your Reaction can protect an ally within 10 feet of you.

*Sealed Seams.* While you wear the suit, you're comfortable in extreme heat and extreme cold, and you automatically succeed on saving throws against Exhaustion from them.

features.name: Flight
features.text: While you wear the suit, you have a Fly Speed equal to your Speed.

features.name: The Map
features.text:
You gain proficiency with Cartographer's Tools; if you already have it, choose another type of Artisan's Tools. You carry a map that draws itself: it shows any place you have spent 10 minutes in, you can't become lost except by magic, and it is your Spellcasting Focus while you hold it.

*Fair Copy.* With Cartographer's Tools and 10 minutes of work, you can copy any map, chart, or plan you've seen, from memory, and you can tell at a glance whether a map is accurate, out of date, or a deliberate lie.

*Folds.* You can fold the map a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus plus 2, and you regain all expended folds when you finish a Long Rest. Fold Space costs one fold; Contour Lines costs two.

*Fold Space.* As a Bonus Action, you expend a fold: a willing creature (it can be you) you can see within 30 feet of yourself teleports up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space you can see.

features.name: Contour Lines
features.text: As a Bonus Action, you expend two folds and draw the ground steeper than it is. Each creature of your choice in a 10-foot-radius Sphere centered on a point you can see within 60 feet of yourself makes a Strength saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, a creature takes Force damage equal to the Arc Gun's dice, has the Prone condition, and has a Speed of 0 until the end of its next turn. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only. (As with Slick, a creature you knock Prone is for the blades, not your Arc Gun.)

features.name: Survey
features.text:
You can spend 10 minutes mapping your surroundings. The map shows every secret door, hidden passage, and trap within 60 feet of you that isn't hidden by magic, and you learn the general nature of each trap.

*Route.* When you plan a journey between two places on your map, you know how long it will take at each travel pace, the safest route and the fastest (rarely the same), and every danger the map has recorded on the way: a ford that floods, a pass that closes, a valley where cattle die.

features.name: Wide Fold
features.text:
When you use Fold Space, you can teleport two willing creatures instead of one, and each can teleport up to 30 feet.

*Longitude.* You always know exactly where you are on the face of the world, latitude and longitude both, and the true time where you stand. A ship you navigate can't become lost except by magic.

features.name: Shortcut
features.text: Once per Long Rest, as a Magic action, you fold the map along a line you've drawn: you and up to two willing creatures within 10 feet of you teleport to a place within 500 feet of you that is on your map. Each arrives in an unoccupied space of your choice there.

multiclass.gains: Hit Point Die, proficiency with Tinker's Tools, and training with Light armor
multiclass.text: You must have an Intelligence score of 13 or higher. Gain the following traits from the Core Mhizha Traits table: Hit Point Die, proficiency with Tinker's Tools, and training with Light armor. Gain the Mhizha's level 1 features, which are listed in the Mhizha Features table. For multiclass spell slots, add half your Mhizha levels (round up), as you would Paladin or Ranger levels. If you have more levels in another class than in this one, you build one device instead of the number shown in the Devices column of the Mhizha Features table, and you make a number of Preparations equal to half your Mhizha levels (round up) instead of your Proficiency Bonus.

data.name: Natural Philosopher
data.blurb: Int. No magic: the laws the world already obeys.

traits.value: *Choose 3:* Arcana, History, Insight, Investigation, Medicine, Nature, Perception, or Survival
Simple weapons, and Martial weapons that have the Ammunition and Loading properties
*Choose 2:* Alchemist's Supplies, Cartographer's Tools, Glassblower's Tools, Navigator's Tools, or Tinker's Tools
*Choose A or B:* (A) Leather Armor, Light Crossbow, 20 Bolts, Crossbow Bolt Case, Dagger, Scholar's Pack, the two tools you chose, and 10 GP; or (B) 150 GP

features.name: Natural Philosophy
features.text:
You know the world by measuring it.

**Study.** As a Bonus Action, or over 1 minute outside combat, you study a creature, an object, or a feature of the environment that you can see within 60 feet of yourself. You can be studying one creature and one object or feature at a time; studying another replaces the earlier one of the same kind. A creature stays studied for 1 minute, and an object or feature until you finish a Short or Long Rest. This isn't the Study action, and it needs no check. When you study something, you learn one of the following of your choice:

- *A creature:* its Armor Class, which of its saving throws has the lowest bonus, one damage Resistance, Immunity, or Vulnerability it has (the DM chooses if it has several, and tells you if it has none), or its Speeds and special senses.
- *An object or a feature:* what it's made of, roughly how old it is, how it was made, or where it's weakest.

Studying something you're already studying renews it and teaches you another fact from the list. You can also study the place around you; from level 3, that's how you find what Mechanism can set off.

You learn only what can be seen, heard, or measured. Study never tells you what a creature thinks or feels.

**Measure.** You can judge, by eye and with the instruments you carry, the distance to anything you can see, its height, its weight, and its temperature, to within a tenth, and the time of day to within a few minutes.

features.name: Ballistics
features.text:
When you make an attack roll with a crossbow or a firearm, you can use your Intelligence modifier instead of your Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls. A firearm is a Pistol, a Musket, or a period firearm such as the pocket pistol (*The Setting*, Characters, Equipment and Firearms); the stonebow is a crossbow.

**Calculated Shot.** Once per turn, when you hit a creature you're studying with an attack roll using a crossbow or a firearm, the attack deals the extra damage shown in the Calculated Shot column of the Natural Philosopher Features table. The extra damage is the same type as the weapon's.

**Weapon Mastery.** You can use the mastery property of one kind of crossbow or firearm you're proficient with, such as Heavy Crossbows or Pistols. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kind you chose. Each one plays differently: a Musket or Light Crossbow slows what it hits, a Heavy Crossbow pushes it (farther, once you learn Leverage), and a Pistol or Hand Crossbow carries Advantage into your next turn, which leaves that turn's Bonus Action free.

features.name: Aim
features.text: When you study a creature on your turn, your next attack roll against it before the end of the turn has Advantage if it's a crossbow or firearm attack that uses your Intelligence (see Ballistics). The Advantage comes from the measuring, not from standing still: move as you like before or after, and take the shot from wherever the angle is. Studying a creature you're already studying counts, so you can Aim at the same target every turn.

features.name: First Causes
features.text:
You can ask why. You spend 1 minute examining something in the physical world, and then ask the DM why it happened or is happening: why the bridge failed, why the well went bad, why the ward keeps flickering. The DM answers with the most likely cause that follows from what can be seen, measured, or tested, in a sentence or two. If what you can examine isn't enough, the DM tells you so, and the use isn't expended. The answer is never about what a creature thinks or feels.

You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Instruments
features.text: Choose two of your tool proficiencies, or one tool proficiency and the Investigation skill (gaining proficiency in Investigation first if you lack it). You have Expertise with your choices.

features.name: Mechanism
features.text:
You turn the place against the people in it, using a law of nature the place already obeys. You need a feature you're studying: a structure under load, a slope, a body of water held back, a fire or a store of powder, a pocket of gas or smoke, a strong light. It has to be part of the place: nothing you or your allies placed, lit, or created there.

**Finding the feature.** When you study the place around you (a Bonus Action, or 1 minute outside combat), the DM names one feature in it you could set off, which laws from the Mechanism table it allows, and what it can reach, and you're now studying that feature. A place worth fighting in has at least one: a chandelier or a beam overhead, a staircase or a slope, a canal or a cistern, a hearth or a powder store, a window in the sun. A rich place (a foundry, a ship's deck, a mill) has two or three, and studying it again finds the next. If a place truly has none, the DM says so, and the study costs you no action. Scouting a room for a minute before the door opens is time well spent.

As a Utilize action, you set off the feature you're studying with one precise act from where you stand: a cut rope, a kicked wedge, an opened sluice, a tipped brazier, an angled lens, or, at a distance, a shot, a thrown stone, or a tug on a line already rigged. Choose one of the laws the DM named for it. Each creature of your choice in a 20-foot Cube that lies within the feature's reach, with its point of origin within 60 feet of you, makes a saving throw (DC 8 plus your Intelligence modifier and Proficiency Bonus). Everything was settled when you studied the place, so nothing waits on a ruling now.

On a failed save, a creature takes the damage shown in the Mechanism column of the Natural Philosopher Features table and suffers the law's effect. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage only. The feature is then spent, though what it leaves behind stays: what's left (rubble, a flooded floor) isn't a new feature until the DM says the place has changed enough to hold one.

You can use this feature five times, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

| Law | The feature | Save | Damage | On a failed save |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Mechanics | A load, a slope, a hanging weight | Dexterity | Bludgeoning | Restrained (pinned) until the end of its next turn. The area becomes Difficult Terrain (rubble). |
| Heat | A fire, a furnace, powder, a sealed vessel | Dexterity | Fire | Pushed 10 feet away from the feature, and has Disadvantage on attack rolls until the end of its next turn, scorched and dazzled. Flammable objects in the area catch fire. |
| Pneumatics | Gas, smoke, foul air | Constitution | Poison | Poisoned until the end of its next turn. The area is Heavily Obscured until the end of your next turn. |
