When you tend a creature through a natural disease over a Long Rest, without ending it with a spell or a feature, it has Advantage on its saving throws against the disease until your next Long Rest; if it recovers, it can't catch that disease again. A disease ended by Treatment counts as the slow way too.

features.name: Outbreak
features.text:
Your afflictions spread. When a creature fails a saving throw against a level 1+ Physician spell you cast that deals Necrotic or Poison damage, or fails its saving throw against your noxious Miasma, it becomes **infected**. The infection is a disease. An infected creature can't regain Hit Points. At the start of each of its turns, it takes Necrotic damage equal to your Intelligence modifier (you can choose for it to take none). At the end of each of its turns, it makes a Constitution saving throw against your spell save DC. On a success, the infection ends. On a failure, one other creature of your choice within 5 feet of it becomes infected. An infection ends after 1 minute if it hasn't ended sooner. No more creatures can be infected at once than your Intelligence modifier (minimum of one); while that many are infected, no other creature becomes infected. Creatures that have Immunity to disease can't be infected, and your allies are never infected by this feature.

In addition, each creature that regains Hit Points from your Miasma has Resistance to Poison damage and can't be diseased until the end of its next turn.

**Tracing.** When you examine a creature that has a natural disease, you learn the route the disease took to it: the water, the air, a touch, the cloth, the food, or the vermin. You can also ask the DM one of the following questions, and the DM answers truthfully. Whom or what did it catch the disease from (if that source is within a day's travel)? Who else here has it? Who or what carried it here?

features.name: Doctor's Rounds
features.text:
The radius of your Miasma becomes 20 feet. In addition, each friendly creature within 10 feet of you has Advantage on Constitution saving throws and has Immunity to disease and to the Poisoned condition.

**Wide Berth.** You can walk into and out of a quarantined city, a cordon, or a pest house, and no guard stops you. A health officer anywhere will take your word on whether a house can be opened, a ship unloaded, or a body buried.

subclasses.name: Surgeon
subclasses.lead: <!-- Scott: the Surgeon's introduction. The Scalpel half of the old shared introduction ("precise magical incisions … on the cutting edge") is in archive/cuts-2026-10-22.md. -->

features.name: Theatre Training
features.text: Your instrument is a Scalpel. It is a Spellcasting Focus for your Physician spells rather than a weapon. You also learn the *Mage Hand* cantrip if you don't already know it. It counts as a Physician cantrip for you and doesn't count against the number of cantrips you know, and the spectral hand takes the shape of your instrument.

features.name: Under the Knife
features.text: When you hit a creature with an incision (described below), you can use Healing Prowess as part of the same attack, without spending a Bonus Action. You expend a Prowess Die as normal. The creature you heal can be any creature within 10 feet of you or within 10 feet of the target. If the target is your patient, it can't take Reactions until the end of its next turn.

features.name: The Incision
features.text: As a Magic action, you can make an **incision**: a ranged spell attack using Intelligence against a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself. On a hit, the target takes 1d10 Force damage. This damage increases to 2d10 at Physician level 5, 3d10 at level 11, and 4d10 at level 17.

features.name: The Sharpest Cut
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, you can send your instrument to hover at a point you can see within 60 feet of yourself, where it stays until you send it again, recall it as a Bonus Action, or have the Unconscious condition. It returns to you if it is ever more than 60 feet from you, and it can't be targeted by attacks, spells, or other effects.

Your incisions now add your Intelligence modifier to their damage. While your instrument hovers, your incisions originate from it rather than from you, and you can use Healing Prowess on any creature within 10 feet of it rather than only a creature you touch.

The hovering instrument can also do anything your *Mage Hand* could do (manipulate an object, open a door or a container, carry up to 10 pounds) using a Bonus Action, without your having to cast the spell. It can use a Healer's Kit, and you can make Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) checks through it, and Intelligence (Medicine) checks to stabilize or examine a creature within 5 feet of it.

features.name: The Sealed Table
features.text:
You add *Telekinesis* and *Resilient Sphere* to your spellbook. They count as Physician spells for you and are always prepared; they don't count against the number of spells you can prepare.

You also learn to seal the table. When you cast *Resilient Sphere*, you can choose to have it enclose you and one willing creature within 5 feet of you together, as though the two of you were a single Large creature. While you are enclosed together, you can perform Treatment on that creature and use Healing Prowess on it as normal; nothing else passes through the sphere in either direction, as the spell describes.

In addition, you can perform Treatment on your patient while it is within 10 feet of your hovering instrument, rather than only within your reach.

features.name: Theatre Closed
features.text: When a creature within 10 feet of you, or within 10 feet of your hovering instrument, would be reduced to 0 Hit Points, you can take a Reaction to declare the theatre closed. Choose the point the triggering creature was within 10 feet of, you or the instrument. Until the start of your next turn, each creature within 10 feet of that point that you choose when you take the Reaction, including the triggering creature, can't be reduced below 1 Hit Point. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Continuity
features.text:
You feel the Font everywhere: in the air you breathe, the ground under you, the sky over you, and every living thing around you, and you feel yourself as part of it. You can't be cut off from it; a cellar, a city, and a dungeon are all alive. The life you pass on runs through you on the way, and you gain the following benefits.

- **Within and Without.** When you restore Hit Points to another creature with a Physician spell or Healing Prowess, you regain Hit Points equal to your Intelligence modifier (minimum of 1). You can benefit from this once on each turn.
- **Nothing Is Wasted.** When Hit Points you restore with a Physician spell or Healing Prowess would raise a creature above its Hit Point maximum, the excess goes instead to another creature of your choice within 30 feet of you that is missing Hit Points (the most injured, unless you choose otherwise); that creature can be you. The excess passes on only once: whatever the second creature can't use is lost. You can't heal a creature that is already at its Hit Point maximum just to send the healing on.
- **The Day Shows.** When you restore Hit Points to a creature, the world around you answers, and does it no harm. The light warms and goes golden, the air thickens and moves, insects hum, birds start up, and the nearest green things lean toward you, bud, or flower; a crack in a wall fills with moss. In November, a garrison's plane trees bud. Anyone watching knows something just happened.

features.name: The Book of the World
features.text:
When you reach a Physician level specified in the Vitalist Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared, and they are in your spellbook. They count as Physician spells for you and don't count against the number of spells you can prepare.

| Physician Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Goodberry*, *Speak with Animals* |
| 5 | *Locate Animals or Plants*, *Speak with Plants* |
| 7 | *Locate Creature*, *Plant Growth* |
| 9 | *Commune with Nature*, *Reincarnate* |

features.name: Signatures
features.text:
You gain proficiency in the Nature skill and with the Herbalism Kit; if you already have either, choose another skill from the Physician's skill list or another tool. By handling a plant, a stone, a fungus, or a part of an animal for 1 minute, you learn its virtues: whether it's poisonous and what it would do, what it heals or harms, and whether it could serve as a component for a spell you know. Given an hour in any place where things grow, you can find the simples for an ordinary remedy, a dye, or a poison.

**Diagnose a Place.** You can use Diagnosis on a place you stand in (a field, a well, a wood, a house): you learn whether it is blighted, poisoned, diseased, or cursed, and whether it is thin ground (*Life on the Border*, Introduction, The Hidden, in the rules).

**Treat a Place.** You can use Treatment on a place you have diagnosed. It takes 1 hour and a use of a Healer's Kit, and the DC is the same as for the affliction in a creature (cure a disease for a blighted field or a sickly herd, end the Poisoned condition for a poisoned well, which needs no check). On a success, the place mends over the next few days. A curse needs magic, as it would in a patient.

**Respectable.** Your magic is natural magic, and to anyone trained to look it reads that way. You have Advantage on any ability check to convince an official, a licensing examiner, or an inquisitor that your magic is lawful.

features.name: The Ground Takes It
features.text: When you or a creature you can see within 30 feet of you takes damage, you can take a Reaction and expend one Prowess Die to let the world take part of it: the damage is reduced by the number rolled plus your Intelligence modifier. Where the hurt goes shows: the grass under the creature browns, a puddle steams, a beam groans.

features.name: The World's Pulse
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, or over a minute outside a fight, you can feel for the pulse of the living world around you. Until the end of your next turn, you know the location of every living creature within 30 feet of yourself, and whether each is unharmed, injured, Bloodied, or near death. A creature that is hidden from you or has the Invisible condition can't hide its location from this sense, and you can't be surprised by a living creature you sensed this way. Undead and Constructs have no pulse: you sense them only as a gap where the life around them stops, which is often how you find them. The range becomes 60 feet at Physician level 10.

This sense needs no sight, and it works through walls, but not through more than a few feet of stone or a sheet of lead.

You also heal through the current. You can use Healing Prowess on any creature within 30 feet of yourself (60 feet from Physician level 10), rather than only a creature you touch, whether or not you are feeling for the pulse.

**The Long Cure.** If you have a weapon, bandage, or other object that carries a creature's blood or wound, you can cast a spell on it that restores Hit Points or ends a condition or disease, and the spell reaches that creature at any distance if it's on the same plane of existence. The spell's casting time becomes 1 hour.

features.name: Nothing Is Lost
features.text:
When Nothing Is Wasted has no creature to send the excess to, the excess stays with the creature you healed as Temporary Hit Points, up to a total equal to your Physician level.

**The Herbal.** When you finish a Long Rest, you can prepare one simple with your Herbalism Kit and give it to anyone. Any creature can take a Utilize action to apply the simple to itself or to a creature within its reach; that creature regains Hit Points equal to one roll of your Prowess Die. The simple loses its virtue at your next Long Rest.

**Almanac.** With a day's observation of a place, you can ask the DM two of the following questions about it, and the DM answers truthfully. Will its harvest be good or poor? Is a sickness season coming, and roughly when? When will its birds, fish, or herds move? What is this place afraid of?

features.name: The Wheel Turns
features.text:
When a creature you can see within 30 feet of you, to which you have restored Hit Points since your last Long Rest, drops to 0 Hit Points but isn't killed outright, you can take a Reaction: the creature drops to 1 Hit Point instead and regains Hit Points equal to your Physician level. Every green thing within 60 feet of you goes through a year in a moment: it buds, flowers, fruits, and drops its leaves. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

**The Great Chain of Being.** When you diagnose a creature, automatically or with a successful check, you also learn its creature type and whether it is a Hidden creature (*Life on the Border*, Introduction, The Hidden, in the rules).

> **Playing a Vitalist**
>
> Heal, and feel it come back: every time you mend someone else, you mend a little yourself. Don't worry about overhealing; whatever a creature can't hold goes on to the next one who needs it, and from 10th level it stays as a cushion. When a blade is about to land on someone near you, let the ground take part of it: that's your Reaction from 3rd level, and the choice in most fights is whether to spend a die on the blow or on the heal. From 6th you needn't touch anyone to heal them, and before a door opens you can feel who's breathing behind it. Out of a fight, you're the one who can diagnose a field, a well, or a herd, and treat it. Open the windows.

multiclass.gains: Hit Point Die, proficiency in the Medicine skill, and training with Light armor
multiclass.text: You must have an Intelligence score of 13 or higher. Gain the following traits from the Core Physician Traits table: Hit Point Die, proficiency in the Medicine skill, and training with Light armor. Gain the Physician's level 1 features, which are listed in the Physician Features table. For multiclass spell slots, add all your Physician levels, as you would Wizard levels. If you have levels in another class, you regain expended Prowess Dice only when you finish a Long Rest.

rows.Class Features: Spellcasting, Vistas, Planar Strike, Planar Adept

features.name: Spellcasting
features.text:
You draw the power of the cosmos through yourself. See the *Player's Handbook* for the rules on spellcasting. The information below details how you use those rules with Revelator spells, which appear in the Revelator spell list later in the class's description.

**Spell Slots.** The Revelator Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

**Prepared Spells of Level 1+.** You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose two level 1 Revelator spells. *Cure Wounds* and *Protection from Evil and Good* are recommended. (*Healing Word* is a Bonus Action, and your Bonus Action is usually spoken for by a vista; *Cure Wounds* gives your action a second use.)

The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Revelator levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Revelator Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional Revelator spells until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

**Changing Your Prepared Spells.** Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one spell on your list with another Revelator spell for which you have spell slots.

**Spellcasting Ability.** Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for your Revelator spells.

**Spellcasting Focus.** You can use Cartographer's Tools, a token carried back from a spirit voyage, or a weapon with which you have proficiency as a Spellcasting Focus for your Revelator spells.

features.name: Vistas
features.text:
*Your glimpse of the greater cosmology awakened something within you, something you can now share with others.*

**Revelations.** Revelations are the planes you know. Each gives one Spirit Aspect and one Influence. You start knowing two, the echoes of the world closest to home: the Hidden and the Ghostlands. Most Revelations are granted by your features by name; two features let you choose one (The Near Planes at level 5 and The Circuit at level 13). The full set is in the Cosmography later in the class's description. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one Revelation you chose with another you're eligible for. Revelations granted by features can't be replaced.

**Favor.** Each Revelation you know grants you its plane's Favor once between rests, unless a feature says it grants it more often: you call on the Favor to open a vista. A Short or Long Rest brings every Favor back.

**Opening a Vista.** As a Bonus Action, you call on the Favor of a Revelation you know and open a vista beside a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself (it can be you), and **let in an Influence**: that Revelation's Influence takes effect on the creature. From Revelator level 3, a vista can call a spirit instead (Visiting Spirit), and the spirit steps through beside the creature you chose.

**Influences.** Unless an Influence says otherwise, it lasts until the start of your next turn.

**Your Open Vista.** A vista stays open for 1 minute, until you open another one, until you dismiss it (no action required), or until you have the Incapacitated condition. Your open vista is the one you opened most recently that is still open; it sets the damage of your Planar Strike.

When a vista or its Influence calls for a saving throw, the DC equals your spell save DC. Whenever a Revelator feature uses your spell save DC or spell attack modifier, it means the ones you use for Revelator spells.

> **Tracking Favors**
>
> Give each plane you know a box. A plane that grants its Favor more than once gets more boxes (the Border Ethereal and your earth end two each; walked planes from 9th level, the Mountain's Arete, and some items add more), never more than three. Tick a box when a plane grants its Favor. When a feature lets you **regain a Favor**, erase a tick from any plane; a Short or Long Rest erases them all.

features.name: Planar Strike
features.text:
When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can replace one of the attacks with a Planar Strike: a melee spell attack against a creature within 5 feet of yourself, or a ranged spell attack against a creature within 60 feet of yourself. On a hit, the target takes damage equal to the dice shown in the Planar Strike column of the Revelator Features table, plus your Wisdom modifier for each of those dice (so 2d12 adds twice your Wisdom modifier). You can make only one Planar Strike on each of your turns, and on a turn when you make one, the plane has your other hand: you can't also make the extra attack of the Light property or the Nick mastery. Planar Strike is magical but isn't a spell; you need a free hand or a hand holding your Spellcasting Focus to make it.

**The Plane's Power.** The damage is the type the Cosmography gives your open vista's Revelation. If you have no vista open, it's Force damage.

features.name: Planar Adept
features.text: You learn two cantrips of your choice from the Revelator spell list. *Guidance* and *Message* are recommended. The chosen cantrips count as Revelator spells for you, and Wisdom is your spellcasting ability for them. Whenever you gain a Revelator level, you can replace one of these cantrips with another cantrip from the Revelator spell list.

features.name: The Border Ethereal
features.text:
*You branch out into the tangible spirit of all things, the Ethereal Plane.*

You know the Revelation of the Border Ethereal. It's the plane you cross most often, and it grants its Favor twice between rests.

**Veilsight.** You can see into the Border Ethereal within 60 feet of yourself, and you can speak with spirits and ghosts as if you shared a language.

features.name: Ethereal Stride
features.text:
*Your familiarity with the Ethereal blossoms.*

As a Bonus Action, you can call on the Favor of the Border Ethereal, or of the Deep Ethereal if you know it, to step into the Border Ethereal until the end of your turn. While there, you can move through creatures and objects as if they were Difficult Terrain, and creatures on the Material Plane can't see you unless they can see into the Ethereal. You can affect and be affected only by things in the Ethereal Plane. Ethereal Stride doesn't open a vista.

**Guiding.** You can bring one willing creature you touch. It enters the Border Ethereal with you, moves with you, staying within 5 feet of you, and returns when you do.

You return to the Material Plane when the stride ends. If you would arrive inside an object or creature, you are shunted to the nearest unoccupied space and take 1d10 Force damage. The same applies to any creature you guide.

features.name: Visiting Spirit
features.text:
When you open a vista, you can **call a spirit** instead of letting in an Influence. A spirit of that plane steps through into an unoccupied space next to the creature you chose. It uses the Visiting Spirit stat block, with that Revelation's Spirit Aspect.

You can have one spirit at a time, and it doesn't require Concentration. It stays for 1 hour, until it drops to 0 Hit Points, until you call another spirit, until you dismiss it (no action required), or until you have the Incapacitated condition. If a spirit you called drops to 0 Hit Points, you can't call any spirit again until you finish a Short or Long Rest; you can still let in Influences.

**A Guest, Not a Soldier.** The spirit is an ally to you and your companions, but it doesn't fight: it can't make attack rolls, and it doesn't deal damage. It has no turn of its own; it acts on yours. At any point on each of your turns, you can move it up to its Speed (no action required), and it takes the Help action or, if you choose, the Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Hide, Search, or Utilize action. You decide its Reaction.

**Commanding the Spirit.** While the spirit is within 100 feet of you, you can command it with a Bonus Action, and the vista that calls it also commands it; letting in an Influence doesn't. When commanded, the spirit uses its Aspect's power at once. The command comes on top of its action: a commanded spirit still moves and Helps that turn.

**Speaking Across.** While the spirit is within 100 feet of you, you can communicate with it telepathically. As a Bonus Action, you can see through its eyes and hear what it hears until the start of your next turn, gaining any special senses it has.

> **Visiting Spirit**
>
> *Small or Medium creature (your choice) of the type its Spirit Aspect names, Neutral*
>
> **AC** 12 + your Wisdom modifier
>
> **HP** 5 + your Revelator level
>
> **Speed** 30 ft.
>
> | STR | DEX | CON | INT | WIS | CHA |
> |---|---|---|---|---|---|
> | 10 | 14 | 10 | 10 | 12 | 10 |
>
> **Saving Throws** use your saving throw bonuses
>
> **Senses** Darkvision 60 ft.; Passive Perception 11
>
> **Languages** understands the languages you know
>
> ***Aspect.*** It gains the Spirit Aspect of the Revelation that called it, including its creature type. Effects that depend on creature type, such as *Protection from Evil and Good* or *Banishment*, treat the spirit as that type. When an Aspect calls for a saving throw, the DC equals your spell save DC.

> **For the DM: The Spirit Is a Guide**
>
> A Visiting Spirit helps, scouts, and carries, and it isn't there to take hits for the party. Play it like a familiar: enemies swat it when it's in their way or when it's obviously helping, and otherwise ignore it.

features.name: Revelator Pathway
features.text: You gain a Revelator subclass of your choice: the pathway that called you on your spirit voyage. The Bridge, the River of Life, the Mountain, the River of Death, and the Tree are detailed after this class's description. Each pathway spans the Veil from earth to sky: at level 3 you learn its earth end, where it touches the Deep Ethereal, and at levels 7 and 15 its Outer Planes. Your earth end is the plane you know best, and it grants its Favor twice between rests. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your pathway's features that are of your Revelator level or lower; the Tree also has one at level 5.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Revelator levels 8, 12, and 16.

features.name: The Near Planes
features.text:
*Your soul expands to encompass the energetic planar sources.*

You learn one Revelation of your choice from the Cosmography's Near Planes: Positive Energy, Negative Energy, the Deep Ethereal, or the Elemental Planes.

features.name: The Crossings
features.text:
*The spirit and soul meet the mind.*

You know the Revelation of the Astral.

**Wayfinder.** You can't become lost by magical means, and you always know the direction to the nearest portal, curtain, or color pool on the plane you're on. You have Advantage on Intelligence checks to recall lore about the planes and their inhabitants.

features.name: Guide's Hand
features.text:
*Your experience allows you to help others traveling with you.*

**Many Travelers.** When you use Ethereal Stride, you can guide a number of willing creatures equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one), each of whom you touch or who is within 5 feet of a creature you guide.

**Hold the Threshold.** When a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself fails a Death Saving Throw, or suffers a failure by taking damage while it has 0 Hit Points, you can take a Reaction and call on the Ghostlands' Favor to turn one of those failures into a success. This doesn't open a vista.

features.name: Reach Beyond
features.text:
*You can push through to the deepest, most well-guarded parts of reality, if you're brave enough.*

Once per Long Rest, as a Bonus Action, you can open a vista without calling on a Favor, reaching instead for any Revelation in the Cosmography that you don't know. You can do this even when every plane's Favor is spent. A reach within the Cosmography draws no Attention.

**Past the Map.** Instead, you can reach past the Cosmography, toward what it leaves out: a single layer or realm, such as the efreet's city in the Plane of Fire or a god's hall in Valhalla; a ruler and their court, such as an archfey, Yama with his scribe, the Jade Emperor in his palace, the lord of the deepest circle of the Nine, or a demon lord in their layer; or what lies between and beyond, such as the dead gods adrift in the Astral, the crossroads of the Middle World, or the Far Realm. The vista both calls a spirit and lets in an Influence, and the Influence affects every creature of your choice within 30 feet of the vista. The DM decides what comes through from that place's nature, taking the Cosmography's Aspects and Influences as the yardstick: the nearest plane's, bent toward the place you reached. A reach past the map always draws Attention.

**The Strain.** The further you reach, the more passes through you, and the body you left behind has to bear it. Reaching past the Cosmography forces you to make a Constitution saving throw: DC 15 for a particular layer or realm, or DC 20 for a god, a ruler, or the Far Realm. On a failed save, you take 6d6 Psychic damage (10d6 against DC 20); on a successful save, you take half as much damage. If you fail the DC 20 save, your spirit also takes the long way home: you can't call on any plane's Favor until you finish a Short or Long Rest. You can still Strike, cast spells, and command whatever came through. Either way, the vista opens, and you get what you reached for.

**Attention.** A power of that place notices you, and you have its Attention. The DM decides what the power guards and what it wants from you; it might call in a favor, pay you a visit, set you a test, or name a debt. Powers act from their nature, not from malice, but not necessarily kindly. The debt is the cost, and it is paid in story, not in Favors. While you have a power's Attention, using Reach Beyond on its place again deepens the relationship rather than drawing new Attention.

features.name: Soul's Journey
features.text:
*Your soul never forgets your travels, for better and for worse.*

A Revelation you know is **walked** once you have been to that plane in the body, spent at least a Long Rest there, and come back. How you got there doesn't matter: by portal, by another's spell, by being taken, by walking in for the name of it, or by waking up there. The plane cares only that you stayed, and what it does to those who stay is the lesson (see "What the Walk Costs," in "Walking the Planes" after the Cosmography). A plane you walked before you knew its Revelation is walked the moment you learn it.

A walked plane knows you: it grants its Favor twice between rests. Walking a plane that already grants its Favor twice, such as your earth end or the Border Ethereal, adds nothing.

**The First Voyage.** When you gain this feature, one Revelation you know, other than your earth end or the Border Ethereal, counts as walked: the place your first voyage took you, back when you walked the Wheel in spirit.

**The Hard Roads.** Seven places on the Wheel are walked by almost no one, and walking one leaves a mark for life. They're described in "Walking the Planes," after the Cosmography.

features.name: Wider Vistas
features.text: When you let in an Influence, you can choose a second creature (it can be you) you can see within 30 feet of the vista. The Influence affects both creatures.

features.name: The Circuit
features.text:
*You understand the shape of the world.*

You learn one Revelation of your choice from the Cosmography's Near Planes, Circuit at Level 7, Borderlands, or Dominions. It can be a plane another pathway grants at level 7. The planes the pathways reach at level 15 are beyond you until The Circuit Made Whole. Before The Circuit Made Whole, The Circuit is the only way to learn:

- **The Borderlands:** the planes in the shadow of the Dominions: Arcadia and the House of Song on either side of the Seven Heavens, Gehenna beside the Nine Circles, Pandemonium beside the Abyss. The roads pass through them (the River of Death rises in Pandemonium and runs past Gehenna, and the Bridge crosses Arcadia on its way down from the House of Song), but no pathway stops there. By now you know the roads through them anyway.
- **The Dominions' Quiet Corners:** the Sphere of the Moon, Cocytus, and the Seven Gates.

features.name: Ethereal Wayfarer
features.text:
*The body starts to learn the lessons of the soul.*

**Long Stride.** Ethereal Stride can last up to 1 minute (Concentration, as if it were a spell) instead of until the end of your turn, and you can end it as a Bonus Action. Creatures you guide stay in the Border Ethereal with you for the duration, and any of them can return to the Material Plane as a Bonus Action.

**Etherealness.** You can cast *Etherealness* without expending a spell slot. When you do, you can bring a number of willing creatures within 10 feet of you equal to your Wisdom modifier (minimum of one). Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: The Body Follows
features.text:
*The last aspect of your material form joins you.*

You can cast *Plane Shift* without expending a spell slot or Material components. It can take you only to the Material Plane or to a plane whose Revelation you know, and you arrive exactly where you intend. You can't use this casting to send an unwilling creature to another plane. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Ethereal Sight
features.text:
*Your senses expand with your new perspective.*

Your Veilsight extends to 120 feet, and you and your spirits can see Invisible creatures and objects within that range.

features.name: Epic Boon
features.text: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Spell Recall is recommended.

features.name: The Circuit Made Whole
features.text:
*You understand why the world is the shape that it is.*

You gain the following benefits.

**Every Revelation.** You know every Revelation in the Cosmography. You can call on any plane's Favor, but on no more than nine different planes between rests. Your earth end still grants its Favor twice, and Arete, if you have it, still works.

**Old Acquaintance.** You can use Reach Beyond twice per Long Rest.

**Favor in the Moment.** When you roll Initiative, you regain up to two Favors.

**Spirit of Totality.** When you call a spirit, you can call the Spirit of Totality instead: a spirit of no one plane, sent by all of them together. It is still your one spirit (with The Fare, it counts as both of your spirits), and it uses the Visiting Spirit stat block. It counts as every creature type, and it understands and speaks every language, but it has no Aspect's traits. When you command it, it uses the commands of two different Spirit Aspects of your choice; a command that needs a trait it lacks (such as an element or its light) can't be chosen. While it's with you, each time you hit with your Planar Strike you can choose its damage type from any plane's.

**Walked Whole.** The hard roads add up. For every two hard roads you have walked, Favor in the Moment regains one more Favor. If you have walked all seven, you also have Advantage on the Constitution saving throw for the Strain of Reach Beyond.

> **Playing a Revelator**
>
> You see the world's other rooms, and each turn you open a door to one. In a fight, attack or cast with your action and open the vista the moment needs with your Bonus Action: its Influence lands on the creature beside it, and your Planar Strike hits with that plane's power. Spend Favors where they count; a Short Rest brings them all back, so a party that rests often lets you be generous. Your spirit doesn't fight: send it where it helps, as a guide, a scout or a voice in the right ear, and move it every turn. Ethereal Stride is your exit and your shortcut: step through the wall, and bring a friend. Out of a fight, you talk with ghosts, see into the Border Ethereal and know the planes better than anyone at the table. Learn what each Influence does, and you'll always have the right door to open.

subclasses.name: The Bridge
subclasses.lead:
*Endure What You Are Commanded to Endure*

A long stretch of paved road, better kept in some places than others. It comes down from the House of Song's workshops, through Arcadia's orchards and the gears of the Celestial Bureaucracy, and ends at a bridge over the River of Death in Acheron. On the far bank, the road becomes the field. The Wheel draws the bridge in Acheron; a Revelator knows its near end, the Bridgehead, stands in the Deep Ethereal, and starts there. Every other road wanders; this one runs straight, and where it meets water it doesn't stop: it builds. A bridge is a road laid over water, the oldest proof that nature can be measured and crossed. Revelators of the Bridge know the road is the first act of resistance to chaos, and they tramp it down.

features.name: Bridge Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Revelator level specified in the Bridge Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spell prepared.

| Revelator Level | Spell |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Compelled Duel* |
| 5 | *Zone of Truth* |
| 9 | *Slow* |
| 13 | *Stoneskin* |
| 17 | *Geas* |

features.name: The Bridgehead
features.text: You know the Revelation of the Bridgehead, the near end of the last bridge.

features.name: The Scale
features.text:
Whenever you open a vista, of any plane and for any purpose, you can also Weigh one creature you can see within 30 feet of the vista that isn't your ally. It stays Weighed for 1 minute, and only one creature can be Weighed at a time. Weighing the same creature again just starts the minute over.

Each time a Weighed creature deals damage to you or one of your allies, the scale tips (an attack or effect that damages several of you at once tips it only once), and the creature takes 1d6 Force damage. The first time the scale tips, the creature's Speed also decreases by 10 feet until the Weighing ends. When the Weighed creature's damage to you tips the scale (including damage you take for an ally through Bear the Verdict) and you have at least 1 Hit Point, you regain Hit Points equal to your Wisdom modifier, no more than once between the start of one of your turns and the start of your next. The blows you take for your friends are the ones that feed you. You always know the direction to a Weighed creature on the same plane as you, and it gains no benefit from the Invisible condition against you or your spirits.

features.name: Bear the Verdict
features.text: You gain training with Heavy armor, and you have Advantage on saving throws you make to avoid being moved or knocked Prone. When an ally within 5 feet of you takes damage, you can take a Reaction, after the damage is rolled, to take the damage instead (any other effect still applies to the ally). If the damage came from a Weighed creature, the scale still tips.

features.name: The Celestial Bureaucracy
features.text: You know the Revelation of the Celestial Bureaucracy.

features.name: The Paperwork
features.text: You can read the seals, stamps, and forms of any office, court, or bureaucracy, in any language: you know whether a document is genuine, what office issued it, and what it lets its bearer do. After an hour in a government office, a customs house, or a court's antechamber, you know whom to see, in what order, and what each of them will want.

features.name: Lockstep
features.text: Your spirit stands where you can't. While your spirit is within 100 feet of you, you can use Bear the Verdict when an ally within 5 feet of your spirit takes damage, as if you were in the spirit's space. You take the damage, not the spirit.

features.name: A Heavier Scale
features.text: The scale's weight shifts onto the Weighed. Each time it tips, the creature also has Disadvantage on its next attack roll before the end of its next turn (tips don't stack: one Disadvantage at a time).

features.name: Acheron
features.text: You know the Revelation of Acheron. You've crossed.

features.name: Endure the Sentence
features.text: When you take damage from the Weighed creature through Bear the Verdict, you have Resistance to it.

features.name: Found Wanting
features.text: As a Bonus Action, you pronounce judgment on a Weighed creature whose scale has tipped during this Weighing (its slowed Speed shows it), wherever it is on the same plane as you. It makes a Charisma saving throw. On a failed save, it takes 6d10 Force damage, loses Concentration, and is banished to an empty stretch of the road until the end of its next turn. It then returns to the space it left (or the nearest unoccupied one), having forgotten the last minute: it still knows its enemies, but not where any creature it can't see is. On a successful save, it takes half as much damage. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclasses.name: The River of Life
subclasses.lead:
*Heal Through the River That Never Ends*

The River of Life rises in Elysium, runs through Eden, and pours into Svarga's sea, where whirlpools carry it back to its source. Revelators of the River of Life channel the life-giving waters to heal their allies.

features.name: River of Life Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Revelator level specified in the River of Life Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spell prepared.

| Revelator Level | Spell |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Bless* |
| 5 | *Aid* |
| 9 | *Mass Healing Word* |
| 13 | *Control Water* |
| 17 | *Mass Cure Wounds* |

features.name: The Maelstrom
features.text: You know the Revelation of the Maelstrom.

features.name: Wellsprings
features.text:
*You hold a vista to the River of Life open, allowing its waters to flow through.* As a Bonus Action, you can call on the Maelstrom's Favor to open a Wellspring in a 5-foot Cube within 30 feet of yourself. It holds two draughts, and it lasts for 1 minute or until its draughts are gone; it doesn't require Concentration, and it closes if you have the Incapacitated condition. You have one Wellspring at a time. It's a vista of its own: it doesn't close or replace your open vista, opening another vista doesn't close it, and it never counts as your open vista.

**The Water Follows.** At the start of each of your turns, you can move the Wellspring up to 30 feet to a space you can see (no action required). During combat, when a Bloodied creature you can see enters the Wellspring, starts its turn there, or has the Wellspring moved onto it, you can spend a draught to have that creature regain 1d4 Hit Points (no action required). A Wellspring doesn't heal outside combat.

features.name: The River Runs One Way
features.text: Each turn, you choose heal or hit. On a turn when an Influence you let in or a command you give restores Hit Points or grants Temporary Hit Points, you can't make a Planar Strike. On a turn when you make a Planar Strike, your Influences and commands can't restore Hit Points or grant Temporary Hit Points, though their other effects still happen. Your Wellspring's draughts, Cascade, and No True End are neither Influences nor commands, so they don't count.

features.name: Water-Taken
features.text: You can breathe water. You always know whether water you can see is safe to drink, and if it's fouled (poison, disease, a corpse upstream), which way the fouling came from. The spirits of springs, pools, wells, and rivers know you as one of the water's own, and with your Veilsight they'll talk to you about what they've seen.

features.name: Elysium
features.text: You know the Revelation of Elysium.

features.name: Steady Flow
features.text: A Wellspring's draughts restore 1d6 Hit Points instead of 1d4.

features.name: Clean Water
features.text: Once per Long Rest, you can spend 10 minutes at a well, spring, cistern, or stretch of stream and open the River of Life into it. All the water within 30 feet of you is cleansed of poison and disease, and water drawn from it stays clean for 24 hours.

features.name: Confluence
features.text: Your Wellspring holds three draughts, and it can fill a 10-foot Cube instead of a 5-foot one. A creature that regains Hit Points from it can also end the Poisoned condition on itself.

features.name: What the Water Took
features.text: Once per Long Rest, you can put your hand in a body of water and name a creature or object lost in it within the last year. You learn where it lies, or where it came ashore. If it was a person, you also learn whether they drowned, were taken, or walked out on their own feet, and if they were taken, by what.

features.name: Eden
features.text: You know the Revelation of Eden.

features.name: Cascade
features.text: As a Bonus Action, you can pour your Wellspring into one creature within 5 feet of it. The Wellspring closes, and the creature regains 2d6 Hit Points for each draught it had left.

features.name: The Far Shore
features.text: When a creature dies within sight of you or of your Wellspring, you can tell it the way across (no action required). Its spirit goes on: it doesn't linger as a ghost, and it can't be raised as Undead against its will. This doesn't prevent a spell that returns it to life.

features.name: No True End
features.text: When an ally within 30 feet of you or of your Wellspring drops to 0 Hit Points, you can take a Reaction to have it drop to 1 Hit Point instead. It then regains Hit Points equal to 2d8 plus your Wisdom modifier. A creature can benefit from this only once per Long Rest.

subclasses.name: The Mountain
subclasses.lead:
*Excellence in Everything*

The heart of the earth: the unmoving stone playground of the gods, rising from Asphodel to Svarga with the Middle World on its slopes. Revelators of the Mountain understand the necessity of all things and work to embody excellence in all its forms.

features.name: Mountain Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Revelator level specified in the Mountain Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spell prepared.

| Revelator Level | Spell |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Guiding Bolt* |
| 5 | *Enhance Ability* |
| 9 | *Haste* |
| 13 | *Fabricate* |
| 17 | *Legend Lore* |

features.name: The Foot of the Mountain
features.text: You know the Revelation of the Foot of the Mountain.

features.name: Arete
features.text: You have one extra Favor between rests, which any plane you know can grant (within the limit of three times for one plane); from Revelator level 11, you have two. You can replace a Revelation you chose when you finish a Short Rest, not only a Long Rest.

features.name: Everything Is Next Door
features.text: You gain proficiency with one tool of your choice and learn one language of your choice. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can exchange the tool, the language, or both for others: the Mountain lends; it doesn't give.

features.name: Hundred Hands
features.text: When a creature you can see attacks an ally within 5 feet of your spirit, and your spirit is within 100 feet of you, you can take a Reaction to give the attack roll Disadvantage. Your spirit catches the blow, but it takes nothing for it.

features.name: The Middle World
features.text: You know the Revelation of the Middle World.

features.name: High Places
features.text: When you spend 10 minutes at the top of a hill, tower, mast, or other high place with a wide view, you see the lay of the land for a day's travel around: the roads and rivers, the settlements and their smoke, and anything that's wrong in it (a burned farm, an army's dust, a place where the Veil has worn thin). The DM describes what's there to be seen. You can do this once per Long Rest.

features.name: Many-Turning
features.text: When you open a vista to let in an Influence, your spirit can take on that Revelation's Spirit Aspect, including its creature type, instead of its own, without calling on another Favor. Its current Hit Points and Hit Point maximum don't change, and it changes its Aspect only once per vista.

features.name: Twofold Vista
features.text: When you open a vista to let in an Influence, you can call on the Favor of a second Revelation you know and let in its Influence through the same vista, on the same creature or another within 30 feet of the vista.

features.name: Guest-Friendship
features.text: You always know the customs of hospitality where you are: what to bring, what to refuse, where to sit, and what not to say. You never give offense by accident. While you're someone's guest and have eaten under their roof, you have Advantage on Charisma checks to persuade them.

features.name: Excellence
features.text: Healing and Temporary Hit Points from your Influences increase by your Proficiency Bonus, and an Influence that lasts until the start of your next turn lasts until the end of your next turn instead.

features.name: Svarga
features.text: You know the Revelation of Svarga, the mountain's summit.

features.name: Seen from the Summit
features.text: Once per Long Rest, when you spend an hour studying a person, a place, or an institution (a court, a guild, a city's government, a family), the DM tells you three true things about how it works: who holds it up, what it fears, and what it wants.

features.name: Apotheosis
features.text: As a Bonus Action, you regain a number of Favors equal to half the number in your Revelations column (round up), and for 1 minute you have Advantage on attack rolls for your Planar Strikes. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclasses.name: The River of Death
subclasses.lead:
*Carry Whoever Pays the Fare*

In myth the Styx is the river under the world, circling the land of the dead; on the Wheel it rises in Pandemonium's howling caverns and runs down through the Lower Planes. A Revelator knows it as the River of Death, and knows it rises in the Source Mists, in the Deep Ethereal, and starts there. Revelators of the River of Death ferry souls across its placid surface to aid them.

features.name: River of Death Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Revelator level specified in the River of Death Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spell prepared.

| Revelator Level | Spell |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Bane* |
| 5 | *Blindness/Deafness* |
| 9 | *Feign Death* |
| 13 | *Confusion* |
| 17 | *Modify Memory* |

features.name: The Source Mists
features.text: You know the Revelation of the Source Mists.

features.name: The River Below
features.text: You have Darkvision with a range of 60 feet, or your Darkvision's range increases by 30 feet if you already have it. You can't become lost underground, and you always know the direction to the nearest water that flows beneath the ground.

features.name: The Fare
features.text: When you call a spirit, you can keep the spirit you already have instead of dismissing it, letting you have two Visiting Spirits at once. Both act on your turn. When you command your spirits, only one of them uses its Aspect. If you call a spirit while you have two, you choose which one leaves.

features.name: Blood in the Pit
features.text: *Your spirits remember the taste of blood.* Once per turn, when you hit a creature with Planar Strike, you can expend one of your Hit Point Dice. Roll it, and add the number rolled to the damage.

features.name: Asphodel
features.text: You know the Revelation of Asphodel.

features.name: Last Rites
features.text: When you see a corpse, you know how long ago it died, and whether its spirit has gone on, lingers nearby, or is being kept from going. You know the funeral customs of any people whose dead you have seen buried, and the dead of those peoples take you seriously: you have Advantage on Charisma checks with spirits of the dead.

features.name: The Unpaid
features.text: When you open a vista, you can let in the Unpaid instead of calling a spirit or letting in an Influence: the shades who couldn't afford the fare. They fill a 15-foot-radius area centered on the vista for 1 minute. The area is Difficult Terrain for your enemies, and an enemy that starts its turn there must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or take 1d6 Psychic damage (2d6 from Revelator level 11, 3d6 from level 15) and have Disadvantage on its next attack roll. The Unpaid stay for the full minute even if the vista closes. Letting them in doesn't dismiss your spirits, and they don't count against your limit of spirits, but only one crowd of the Unpaid can be in the world at a time.

features.name: Full Passage
features.text: When you command your spirits, both can use their Aspects. When you use Blood in the Pit, you can expend two Hit Point Dice instead of one.

features.name: Tartarus
features.text: You know the Revelation of Tartarus.

features.name: The Ferryman
features.text: The Ferryman's skiff slides out of the mist. As a Bonus Action, you call the Ferryman for 1 minute. At the end of each of your turns while he's present, he can carry up to three willing creatures within 30 feet of you, teleporting each to an unoccupied space you can see within 60 feet of yourself. The Charmed and Frightened conditions end on any creature he carries; it forgets what charmed or frightened it. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclasses.name: The Tree
subclasses.lead:
*Fight With the Dead at Your Back*

The World Ash rises from the wells of Asphodel, and its branches reach through Valhalla, Limbo, and Eden. Revelators of the Tree leap into the gleeful fray with the warrior souls they summon urging them on.

features.name: Tree Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Revelator level specified in the Tree Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spell prepared.

| Revelator Level | Spell |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Heroism* |
| 5 | *Magic Weapon* |
| 9 | *Crusader's Mantle* |
| 13 | *Grasping Vine* |
| 17 | *Tree Stride* |

features.name: The Wells
features.text: You know the Revelation of the Wells.

features.name: Tyr's Hand
features.text: *The bravest of the Aesir has one hand, and he put the other where it went on purpose.* You gain proficiency with Martial weapons and a Fighting Style feat of your choice (see the *Player's Handbook*). Your training includes weapon mastery: you can use the mastery properties of two kinds of Simple or Martial weapons of your choice, and whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change the kinds you chose. When you attack with a weapon whose mastery property you can use, you can use your Wisdom modifier instead of your Strength or Dexterity modifier for the attack and damage rolls.

features.name: Into the Fray
features.text: When you command your spirit, you can swap places with it if it's within 30 feet of you. You and the spirit each teleport into the other's space.

features.name: Extra Attack
features.text: You can attack twice instead of once whenever you take the Attack action on your turn.

features.name: Valhalla
features.text: You know the Revelation of Valhalla.

features.name: The Mead-Bench
features.text: Soldiers, mercenaries, sailors, and any other company that drinks together before a fight take you for one of their own after an evening in their company. They'll share their rumors, their billets, and their grievances with you, and in any town with a garrison or a harbor, you can find a bed among them for the night at no cost.

features.name: Rise Each Dawn
features.text: When you drop to 0 Hit Points and don't die outright, your spirit, if you have one, can fall in your place: it drops to 0 Hit Points (so you can't call another until you finish a Short or Long Rest), and you drop to 1 Hit Point instead. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Falcon Cloak
features.text: *Freyja's feather-cloak is lent to you, as it was to Loki.* When you command your spirit, you can teleport to an unoccupied space within 5 feet of it, wherever it is within 100 feet of you, instead of swapping places with it. While you're within 5 feet of your spirit, creatures can't make Opportunity Attacks against you.

features.name: Limbo
features.text: You know the Revelation of Limbo.

features.name: Rise Together
features.text: Rise Each Dawn recharges when you finish a Short or Long Rest. When an ally you can see within 30 feet of yourself drops to 0 Hit Points and doesn't die outright, you can take a Reaction to spend Rise Each Dawn on that ally instead, if you have a spirit: your spirit falls in the ally's place, and the ally drops to 1 Hit Point.

multiclass.gains: Hit Point Die, proficiency in one skill of your choice from the Revelator's skill list, and training with Light and Medium armor and Shields
multiclass.text: You must have a Wisdom score of 13 or higher. Gain the following traits from the Core Revelator Traits table: Hit Point Die, proficiency in one skill of your choice from the Revelator's skill list, and training with Light and Medium armor and Shields. Gain the Revelator's level 1 features, which are listed in the Revelator Features table. For multiclass spell slots, add half your Revelator levels (round up), as you would Ranger levels. Your Revelations and your Planar Strike dice come only from your Revelator levels. If you have levels in another class and fewer than five Revelator levels, you can call a spirit with Visiting Spirit only once, and you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

data.name: Danae
data.blurb: Cha full caster. The fae, and the Hidden’s courts.

traits.value: *Choose 2:* Arcana, Deception, History, Intimidation, Nature, Persuasion, Religion, or Sleight of Hand

*Choose 2:* Calligrapher's Supplies, Cartographer's Tools, Gaming Set, Glassblower's Tools, Herbalism Kit, Jeweler's Tools, Mason's Tools, Musical Instrument, Navigator's Tools, Painter's Supplies, Weaver's Tools, or Woodcarver's Tools
*Choose A or B:* (A) Leather Armor, 2 Daggers, Quarterstaff, Arcane Focus (crystal), Explorer's Pack, and 16 GP; or (B) 50 GP.

rows.Class Features: The Elder Cycles, The Door Opens

features.name: Spellcasting
features.text:
Danae learn their spells through dream. Each night, the Hidden speaks to them deep in sleep, and when they wake, they know what magic to prepare.

**Cantrips.** You know three cantrips of your choice from the Danae spell list. Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can replace one of your cantrips with another cantrip of your choice from the Danae spell list. When you reach Danae levels 4 and 10, you learn another cantrip of your choice from the Danae spell list, as shown in the Cantrips column of the Danae Features table.

**Cantrip Damage.** When you cast a Danae cantrip that rolls only one damage die, add your Charisma modifier to the damage it deals to one target. Once your cantrips roll two or more dice (from character level 5), the extra dice take its place.

**Spell Slots.** The Danae Features table shows how many spell slots you have to cast your level 1+ spells. You regain all expended slots when you finish a Long Rest.

**Prepared Spells of Level 1+.** You prepare the list of level 1+ spells that are available for you to cast with this feature. To start, choose four level 1 spells from the Danae spell list. The number of spells on your list increases as you gain Danae levels, as shown in the Prepared Spells column of the Danae Features table. Whenever that number increases, choose additional spells from the Danae spell list until the number of spells on your list matches the number in the table. The chosen spells must be of a level for which you have spell slots.

If another Danae feature gives you spells that you always have prepared, those spells don't count against the number of spells you can prepare with this feature, but those spells otherwise count as Danae spells for you.

**Changing Your Prepared Spells.** Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can change your list of prepared spells, replacing any of the spells there with other Danae spells for which you have spell slots.

**Spellcasting Ability.** Charisma is your spellcasting ability for your Danae spells.

**Spellcasting Focus.** You can use an Arcane Focus, or any tool from the Danae's tool list or your subclass's tool that you have proficiency with, as a Spellcasting Focus for your Danae spells: the work of your hands is where the Wyrd, the Hidden's weaving of what comes to pass, comes through.

features.name: The Sight
features.text: You see the Hidden's layer over the world. You can see thresholds between worlds within 30 feet of yourself. (A threshold is a fixed place where the waking world touches another realm, such as the Hidden; the DM decides where they lie.) You also know when a creature or an object you can see is under an illusion or a shape-changing effect, or has the Fey creature type, and whether it is a Hidden creature. You gain proficiency in the Insight and Perception skills (if you already have proficiency in either, choose another skill from the Danae's skill list), and you know Sylvan, the Hidden's own speech.

features.name: Warps
features.text:
Once you see the true shape of reality, you can bend its space.

As a Bonus Action, you warp a 5-foot Cube you can see within 60 feet of yourself into one of the shapes below. The warp lasts for 1 minute, until you dismiss it (no action required), or until you unravel it. You can make a number of warps equal to the number in the Warps column of the Danae Features table, and you regain all expended warps when you finish a Short or Long Rest. A warp you keep in place through a rest stays expended until it ends.

Warps don't require Concentration, and they don't choose sides: a warp affects every creature alike, unless its season says otherwise. Warps can't overlap: no part of a warp's space can be part of another warp's space. A warp is a visible thing: a creature that can see its space can tell that the space is wrong, though not what the warp does until it's inside. When a warp calls for a saving throw, the DC equals your spell save DC.

- **Stretch.** Every foot of movement inside the warp costs 2 extra feet. This doesn't stack with Difficult Terrain: inside a Stretch, each foot costs 3 feet either way.
- **Gate.** Your Gates are linked in a chain, in the order you made them; the last leads back to the first. A Gate must rest on a surface. A creature that moves into a Gate of its own will steps out of the next one in the chain, in its space or the nearest unoccupied space to it. A Gate doesn't send on a creature put into it any other way (moved against its will, or caught in a Gate made on it). This costs no movement and doesn't trigger the Gate it arrives in. When you make a Gate and have no other Gate in place, you make two, linked, for one warp: put the second on another surface you can see within 60 feet of yourself. Later Gates join the chain. If a Gate ends, the chain closes around the gap: the Gate before it leads to the Gate after it. A Gate left alone leads nowhere.

**On a Creature.** You can make a warp where creatures are standing. Each creature in the Cube makes a Dexterity saving throw. On a success, it moves to the nearest unoccupied space outside the warp (this doesn't provoke Opportunity Attacks) and isn't affected. On a failure, it's inside the warp, and it enters the warp at the start of its next turn: the warp and its season (see The Half) take it then, as if it had just walked in. You can make a warp on a creature only once on each of your turns.

**Unraveling.** Some features let you unravel a warp. To unravel a warp, you either end one of your warps that is in place or expend one you haven't used yet; either way, the feature takes effect. A feature that tells you to expend a warp uses one you haven't used yet.

**Magic and Travel.** Warps are magical effects: *Detect Magic* reveals them, and *Dispel Magic* ends one as if it were a level 1 spell. Passing through a Gate, or any warp that takes a creature from one space to another without crossing the space between, is teleportation; a push or a fall is not. A creature can travel through your warps this way (Gates, and a Crossing Danae's Doors and Seams) only once per turn.

**Arriving by Teleport.** A creature teleported into a warp's space enters the warp, just as if it had walked in, but a Gate it arrives in doesn't send it on. A creature can't arrive inside a stone's solid space (a Shaping Danae's warp; see Shaping); it arrives in the nearest unoccupied space instead. If nothing in that space would hold a creature standing (the warp hangs in the air or over a drop), the creature instead arrives in the nearest unoccupied space where it can stand, and it doesn't enter the warp. A creature passing through a pair of Doors (a Crossing Danae's warp; see Crossing) follows the Doors' own rules instead.

features.name: Denial
features.text:
You refuse the outcome others would have for you, and change things accordingly.

When a creature you can see hits you with an attack roll while you aren't wearing Medium or Heavy armor or using a Shield, you can take a Reaction and unravel one of your warps to deny it. You gain a bonus to AC against that attack, which can turn the hit into a miss: +3, rising to +4 at Danae level 9 and +5 at level 17.

How reality rearranges itself follows your nature, and from level 3 your subclass:

| | The blow is denied by |
|---|---|
| Before level 3 | a flicker of the Hidden: a scent of rain, a wrong-colored light, and the blow goes wide |
| Binding | a thread that catches the weapon an inch short |
| Changing | a hidden current pulling at them |
| Crossing | the air folding, and the blow arriving somewhere you aren't |
| Naming | a word: the blow is named a miss |
| Shaping | stone or crystal rising across the skin |

features.name: The Half
features.text:
You lean toward one half of the Hidden's year. Choose the light half or the dark half. The light half's seasons are spring and summer; the dark half's, autumn and winter. Your Half is yours, not the calendar's: it never changes with the date or the tide.

**Seasons.** You learn your half's two seasons. When you make a warp, you can give it one season you know. A creature that enters a seasoned warp for the first time on a turn, or starts its turn there, is subject to its season, making any saving throw against your spell save DC. A creature is subject to the season of only one of your warps per turn: the first that takes it.

| Half | Season | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Light | **Spring** | *Strength saving throw.* On a failed save, you move the creature up to 15 feet horizontally in a direction of your choice. A willing creature can instead teleport up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space it can see. |
| Light | **Summer** | The creature takes 1d6 Fire damage. Creatures you choose when you make the warp are immune. The damage increases by 1d6 when you reach Danae levels 5 (2d6), 11 (3d6), and 17 (4d6). |
| Dark | **Autumn** | *Wisdom saving throw.* On a failed save, choose one: the creature has the Charmed condition, with you as the charmer, until the start of its next turn, or it has Disadvantage on the next saving throw it makes before the end of your next turn. |
| Dark | **Winter** | *Constitution saving throw,* made only when the creature enters the warp, not when it starts its turn there. On a failed save, the creature's Speed is 0 and it can't take Reactions until the start of its next turn. |

features.name: Flee
features.text:
When you take damage and are Bloodied afterward but not at 0 Hit Points (whether or not you were Bloodied before), you can take a Reaction to step half out of the world. Unravel one or more of your warps, in place (lots and knots included) or not yet used. You're **Away** for 1 minute, and you gain Temporary Hit Points equal to your Danae level plus 5 for each warp you unraveled. These Temporary Hit Points replace any you already have.

Being Away ends early when you have none of its Temporary Hit Points left, when you have the Incapacitated condition, or when you end it (no action required). While you're Away, you keep your mind and your magic: you cast spells and keep Concentration as normal, and in addition:

- **Half Here.** Attack rolls against you have Disadvantage.
- **Flicker.** Once on each of your turns, you can teleport up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space you can see (no action required).

**Readjust.** When you stop being Away, you come back not quite when you left: at the end of the current turn, you can teleport up to 15 feet to an unoccupied space you can see, and you can't take Reactions until the end of your next turn.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Danae Subclass
features.text: Your prime modality manifests. You gain a Danae subclass of your choice: Binding, Changing, Crossing, Naming, or Shaping. A subclass is a specialization that grants you features at certain Danae levels. For the rest of your career, you gain each of your subclass's features that are of your Danae level or lower.

features.name: Ability Score Improvement
features.text: You gain the Ability Score Improvement feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. You gain this feature again at Danae levels 8, 12, and 16.

features.name: Fae Weaving
features.text:
The Wyrd flows through your hands, giving you what you need in the moment.

Whenever you finish a Long Rest, you can weave fae material into the world with a tool you have proficiency with from the Danae's tool list or your subclass's tool. You create up to a number of nonmagical objects equal to your Proficiency Bonus. Each must be something that tool could make, Medium or smaller, not a consumable (food, a potion, an oil, a poison, or the like) and not ammunition, and worth no more than 10 GP × your Danae level. A tool that makes nothing under the crafting rules weaves the small things of its trade: a Gaming Set dice, cards, and boards; a Musical Instrument strings, reeds, and pipes; Thieves' Tools picks, keys, and wires. The objects are real and work as the real thing, but anyone who handles one feels that it is strange. They come undone when you next finish a Long Rest or when you use this feature again.

**Fairy Gold.** The objects are fairy gold: any of them turns to dross when it changes hands for value, and none can be used as a Material component that has a cost.

features.name: The First Cycles
features.text:
Your warps can be 5-foot or 10-foot Cubes, and you learn two more shapes:

- **Tilt.** You choose which way is down within the warp when you make it. A creature that enters the warp for the first time on a turn, or starts its turn there, makes a Strength saving throw. On a failed save, it is thrown 10 feet that way, stopping if it strikes something solid, and has the Prone condition; a creature thrown upward then falls. A willing creature can instead walk through the warp with down where you chose it: up a wall or across a ceiling, as if it were floor. When the warp ends, down is down again, and a creature left in the air falls.
- **Pocket.** The warp is bigger inside than out. A creature enters it by moving into its space, and a creature inside can leave by spending 5 feet of movement to appear in an unoccupied space next to it. Up to eight Medium creatures fit inside it, whatever its size (a Small or Tiny creature counts as one, a Large creature as four, and a Huge or larger creature can't enter; nor can a creature that wouldn't fit beside those already inside), and anything inside has Total Cover against anything outside, and the reverse. When a Pocket ends, each creature inside it appears in the nearest unoccupied space.

**The Way Back.** You learn the way home: you regain the use of Flee when you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Reading the Season
features.text:
The Hidden settles in you, and you begin to read people as it reads them, by their weather. As a Bonus Action, choose a number of creatures you can see within 30 feet of yourself, up to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one). The DM tells you each one's temper and what lies under it (see Tempers, below). Each of them is **read** by you for 1 hour. You have Advantage on Wisdom (Insight) checks against a creature you've read, and on Charisma (Deception, Intimidation, or Persuasion) checks against it that play to its temper. Other features of yours refer to creatures you've read.

**Tempers.** Every creature has a temper, which is always one of the four seasons. The DM assigns it, and says how long it holds, by the Tempers rule in "The Hidden, in the rules" in this book's introduction.

features.name: Open Book
features.text: You can cast *Detect Thoughts* without expending a spell slot a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. A creature you've read has Disadvantage on its saving throw against the spell.

features.name: The Door Ajar
features.text: While you're Away, when you teleport with Flicker, you can leave a warp of any shape you know in the space you left. It follows every rule for your warps (it can't overlap another, it lasts 1 minute, it can carry a season you know, and it counts as one of your warps in place), except that it costs no Bonus Action and no warp.

features.name: Thresholds
features.text: Your Sight expands, allowing you to see paths into the Hidden itself. You can spend 1 minute at a threshold you can see with The Sight to open it, casting *Plane Shift* without expending a spell slot or needing its Material component. The spell targets you and up to eight willing creatures, it can take you only to or from the Hidden, and you arrive at the threshold's other side. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Loop
features.text:
You learn another warp shape:

- **Loop.** The warp's edges meet. When a creature tries to leave the warp by any means, moving or teleporting, or is moved out of it against its will, it makes a Wisdom saving throw. On a failed save, it steps back in from the opposite side. The movement it spent leaving is lost (as is any spell slot or use the teleport cost), and it can't try to leave that Loop again until its next turn. A creature that succeeds isn't affected by that Loop again.

features.name: The Middle Cycles
features.text: You learn the other half's two seasons. A warp still holds only one season.

features.name: Name the Season
features.text: As a Magic action, you can choose a creature you've read that you can see within 30 feet of yourself. It makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, you turn its temper to another season of your choice for 1 hour; its mood follows, its attitude toward you shifts one step in the direction you choose (Hostile to Indifferent, or Indifferent to Friendly, or the reverse), and it doesn't know it was touched. On a successful save, it knows something tried. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of once), and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: The Hill
features.text:
You learn another warp shape:

- **Hill.** Time inside the warp runs at the hill's pace. A creature that starts its turn inside the warp must succeed on a Wisdom saving throw or, until the start of its next turn, its Speed is halved, it can't take Reactions, and on its turn it can take either an action or a Bonus Action, not both. When a creature leaves a Hill after failing a save against it, it doesn't remember what happened while it was inside.

features.name: Blasé
features.text: The Hidden doesn't let its own be led. You have Immunity to the Charmed and Frightened conditions.

features.name: The Elder Cycles
features.text: You can call the whole year at once. As a Bonus Action, choose a point within 60 feet of yourself. Every creature of your choice in a 30-foot-radius Sphere centered there is subject to all four seasons, making each saving throw separately. A season's effect that would last until the start of a creature's next turn lasts until the end of its next turn instead. To resolve it quickly, each creature rolls its Constitution and Wisdom saving throws together, then its Strength saving throw (summer's damage needs no saving throw). Move the creatures that failed against spring last. This isn't a warp's season: it doesn't count against the one-warp-a-turn limit, and a creature can still be subject to one of your warps' seasons on the same turn. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: The Door Opens
features.text:
When you go Away, you can read up to a number of creatures you can see within 30 feet of yourself equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one), as part of the same Reaction, as if you had used Reading the Season; the DM can tell you their tempers when the fight allows. While you're Away, the door you carry stands open, and you gain these benefits:

- **The Storm.** At the start of each of your turns, choose a season you know. Each creature of your choice in a 15-foot Emanation originating from you is subject to it, and a creature you've read has Disadvantage on any saving throw against it. This counts as one of your warps' seasons, so a creature it takes can't be taken by a warp's season on the same turn. A season's effect that would last until the start of a creature's next turn lasts until the end of its next turn instead.
- **The Glamour Drops.** Each creature you've read that starts its turn within 30 feet of you and can see you makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC (you can spare any of them). On a failed save, it has the Charmed condition, with you as the charmer, until the start of its next turn: it can't bring itself to touch you, and must choose another target if it attacks.

The Storm takes the place of the warps Flicker leaves behind (The Door Ajar): while the door stands open, Flicker still moves you, but leaves no warp.

features.name: Second Sight
features.text: The Sight opens all the way. You have Truesight with a range of 60 feet. When you use Reading the Season, or read creatures as you go Away (The Door Opens), you can read any number of creatures you can see within 60 feet of yourself.

features.name: Epic Boon
features.text: You gain an Epic Boon feat or another feat of your choice for which you qualify. Boon of Fate is recommended.

features.name: Twist of Fate
features.text:
When you roll Initiative, you regain up to two expended warps, and you can then make up to two warps (no action required). Each warp you make this way expends a warp, as usual.

In addition, when a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself fails a saving throw, you can take a Reaction to turn the moment: it succeeds instead. Once you use this benefit, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclasses.name: Binding
subclasses.lead: You learn the arts of binding yourself and others, whether with word, thread, or root.

features.name: Binding Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Danae level specified in the Binding Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Danae Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Command*, *Dissonant Whispers*, *Warding Bond*, *Zone of Truth* |
| 5 | *Bestow Curse*, *Magic Circle* |
| 7 | *Compulsion*, *Phantasmal Killer* |
| 9 | *Dream*, *Planar Binding* |

features.name: Courtly Grace
features.text: You carry yourself as the most elevated of fae nobles. You gain proficiency in one of the following skills of your choice: Deception, Intimidation, Performance, or Persuasion. You have Advantage on Charisma checks you make against a creature that is knotted by you.

features.name: Knots
features.text:
Your warps can be knots. As a Bonus Action, you tie a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself to another creature or to a fixed point within 30 feet of it (the ground, a tree, a door), and speak a geis into the knot. Each unwilling creature you tie makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. If they all succeed, no knot is tied, though the warp is still expended. If you were tying two creatures together and only one succeeds, the other is tied to the ground where it stands instead. A geis binds each unwilling creature in the knot; a willing creature is tied but not bound. An unwilling knotted creature repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, and the knot comes undone on a success. While knotted, it has Disadvantage on saving throws against your warps, its save to end this knot included. Choose the geis:

- **Stay.** It can't willingly move more than 30 feet from what it's tied to.
- **Spare.** It can't willingly target what it's tied to with an attack or a harmful effect.
- **Heed.** It has Disadvantage on attack rolls against anything but what it's tied to. When it attacks something else, it can break the geis instead of taking the Disadvantage.

*Breaking a Geis.* A knotted creature can choose to break its geis when it is about to do what the geis forbids: to walk away, to strike, to turn. If it does, it first takes Psychic damage equal to 2d8 plus your Charisma modifier, and the knot comes undone; then, if it can still act, it does what it chose. The damage increases to 3d8 at Danae level 10 and 4d8 at level 14.

features.name: Kind Words
