features.text:
Your words echo with the terrible grace of the Fair.

When you tie a knot, you can speak to one creature in it that can hear and understand you, as part of the same Bonus Action. It makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, it has your choice of the Frightened or Charmed condition, with you as the source, until the end of its next turn. At the start of any of its turns, the creature can defy you (no action required): it takes the same Psychic damage as breaking a geis, and then the condition ends.

You speak Kind Words once for each knot you tie.

features.name: Heartstrings
features.text: Creatures have Disadvantage on saving throws against your Kind Words. When a creature knotted to another creature fails its save against your Kind Words, you can choose to have the other affected too, without a saving throw; it counts as affected by your Kind Words.

features.name: Handfast
features.text: Outside combat, you can spend 10 minutes tying a binding between two or more willing creatures who make a promise to each other in your presence: a marriage, a contract, an apprenticeship, a truce, a sworn friendship. This costs no warp and isn't a knot for your other features. While the binding holds, each creature in it knows when another breaks the promise, and knows roughly which direction the others lie in, at any distance on the same plane. The binding holds until every creature in it agrees to untie it, or until you untie it. You can keep a number of bindings equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one); tying another unties your oldest.

features.name: Oath
features.text: As a Magic action, choose a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself that is knotted by you or that your Kind Words have affected within the last minute, and name a promise: to yield, to flee, to stand aside, to tell the truth, or not to harm a creature you name. It makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC; a willing creature can choose to fail. On a failed save, the promise binds it for 1 hour. The first time it breaks the promise, it takes 6d10 Psychic damage, and you know. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Thrall
features.text: As a Magic action, you take hold of a creature knotted by you that you can see. It makes a Wisdom saving throw against your spell save DC, with Disadvantage if it has the Charmed or Frightened condition from you. On a failed save, it is under your control until the end of your next turn, as the *Dominate Monster* spell, but the effect doesn't require Concentration. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

subclasses.name: Changing
subclasses.lead: Fate flows through and around you, and you learn to guide the stream.

features.name: Changing Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Danae level specified in the Changing Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Danae Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Augury*, *Bane*, *Bless*, *Enhance Ability* |
| 5 | *Beacon of Hope*, *Clairvoyance* |
| 7 | *Death Ward*, *Divination* |
| 9 | *Commune*, *Contact Other Plane* |

features.name: Lots
features.text:
Your warps can be lots. As a Bonus Action, you ready one: you roll the coin across your knuckles, shake the die, palm the card. A readied lot counts as a warp and, like your other warps, lasts for 1 minute or until you cast it.

When a creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself fails or succeeds on a D20 Test, you can take a Reaction to cast a readied lot on it, and call it:

- **Fair,** when the creature fails. It rolls another d20 and uses the higher roll.
- **Foul,** when the creature succeeds. It rolls another d20 and uses the lower roll.

A lot you cast is spent.

features.name: Flow of Fate
features.text: The stream of fate runs under everyone near you, and you can pull it aside for them as easily as for yourself. When a creature you can see within 30 feet of yourself is hit by an attack roll, you can use Denial for it instead of for yourself, unraveling one of your readied lots; the creature gains the bonus to AC against that attack. Denial's armor restriction applies to you, not to the creature you protect.

features.name: Small Mercies
features.text: Outside combat, when you or a companion goes looking for something ordinary you need (a dropped key, a cheap item a market might stock, a carter going your way, someone who knows the pass), the DM tells you where it turns up, if it can be found anywhere nearby. You can also tell when a game, a lottery, a drawing of lots, or a wager is rigged (marked cards, loaded dice, a fixed draw) by watching one round of it; you don't learn how, only that the house is cheating fate. Once you find something this way, you can't do so again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Losing Streak
features.text: When you call foul and the creature fails the check or saving throw or misses with the attack roll, you regain one expended warp. Once you regain a warp this way, you can't do so again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Road Luck
features.text: While you travel overland or by water with companions, the road's small mishaps don't befall your company unless the DM wants one for the story: no thrown shoe, cracked axle, spoiled flour, or missed tide. Further, when your company's way is uncertain (a fork, a fog, two inns), you can ask the DM which choice the year favors, and the DM answers "this one," "that one," or "neither." Once you ask, you can't ask again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Double or Nothing
features.text: When you ready a lot, you can ready a second as part of the same Bonus Action, expending a warp for each. When you cast a lot on an attack roll and the attack hits, the same call carries to the damage: the attacker rerolls the damage dice and uses the higher total (fair) or the lower (foul).

features.name: Lucky Charm
features.text: Gamblers, sailors, soldiers, midwives, brides, and anyone else who lives by chance can tell what you are after a few minutes in your company. They want you to blow on their dice, touch their nets, and stand at the back of the wedding. You have Advantage on Charisma checks to win over such people, and in any town you can support a Modest lifestyle by being lucky at people, without other work.

features.name: Loaded
features.text: When you cast a lot, instead of calling fair or foul, you can choose the number the roll uses, whether the creature failed or succeeded (if the creature rolled more than one d20, the roll uses only the number you choose). The number counts as rolled: a chosen 20 is a natural 20 (a Critical Hit on an attack roll), and a chosen 1 is a natural 1. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

features.name: Coincidence
features.text: Outside combat, you can let the stream bring you a coincidence. Tell the DM what you need. The DM introduces it in the next scene or soon after, in the form the story allows: the person you were looking for is at the next table, a letter arrives a day early, the ship you missed is still in port because its captain lost at cards. The DM decides the form, and a coincidence never conjures what couldn't plausibly be there. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclasses.name: Crossing
subclasses.lead: A warded door means nothing to you when the wall beside it will do. Walls, floors, and roofs are only more doors, for you and for whoever you bring.

features.name: Crossing Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Danae level specified in the Crossing Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Danae Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Arcane Lock*, *Feather Fall*, *Knock*, *Silence* |
| 5 | *Gaseous Form*, *Nondetection* |
| 7 | *Freedom of Movement*, *Private Sanctum* |
| 9 | *Passwall*, *Teleportation Circle* |

features.name: Doors
features.text:
Your warps can be Doors. As a Bonus Action, you open a pair of linked Doors on solid surfaces you can see within 60 feet of yourself: a wall, a floor, a ceiling, the side of a cart. The pair counts as one warp. Each Door is a 5-foot square, or a 10-foot square from Danae level 5, and a creature fits through it only if the creature's space is no wider than the Door. A creature that moves into one Door of its own will steps out of the other, facing away from its surface; a Door doesn't send on a creature put into it any other way. When a feature refers to a warp's space, a Door's space is the space in front of it, as wide as the Door and 5 feet deep. A Door can open in the floor under a willing creature, which drops through.

*A Door of Your Own.* Your Doors are openings no one has warded. Iron and salt on a house's doors, windows, and chimney don't stop you, or anyone who comes through with you, from passing through a Door you open in its wall, floor, or roof (see "Iron and salt" in the Introduction): the ward stops only crossing an opening, not teleportation past it.

*Inertia.* A creature that falls into a Door comes out of the other still moving. It travels up to the distance it had already fallen, in the direction the far Door faces, before it falls normally or strikes something. When it lands or strikes something, it takes damage as for one fall of the whole distance it fell and traveled, and has the Prone condition if it takes any.

*Keyhole.* One of your Doors can open on a surface you can't see, if it's within 30 feet of yourself and on the far side of a wall, door, floor, or ceiling no more than 5 feet thick (10 feet from Danae level 10). You know whether the space beyond is open before you commit to it.

*Latch.* Once on each of your turns, when you pass through a pair of your Doors that are no more than 30 feet apart, you can latch them behind you: they close, and you regain the warp they used. Doors you leave open for your friends still cost their warp.

*Fellow Travellers.* When you go through one of your Doors, up to a number of willing creatures equal to your Proficiency Bonus within 5 feet of you can go through with you, arriving in unoccupied spaces within 5 feet of the far Door. For each of them, this counts as its one trip through your warps that turn.

features.name: Back Ways
features.text: You gain proficiency in the Stealth skill (if you already have it, choose another skill instead). After you spend a day in a settlement, you know its back ways: you can find a route between any two places in it that avoids its main streets, watch posts, and toll gates, if such a route exists. After you spend an hour in a building, you know every way into and out of it that a person could use (doors, windows, chimneys, drains, the servants' stair), even the ones its owner has forgotten, and where its walls are thin enough for a Door.

features.name: Seams
features.text: Every warp that fills a space is a Gate for you, whatever its shape: when you enter one of your warps, you can step out of any other (once per turn, as for all travel through your warps). While you're in one of your warps, you can take the Hide action as a Bonus Action on a turn you haven't made an attack roll, and you can hide there without cover and even while an enemy can see you. Hiding this way ends when you leave the space of your warps, unless you leave by travelling through one of them.

features.name: Where No One Follows
features.text: When you travel through one of your warps, you don't provoke Opportunity Attacks for the rest of that turn, and you can close the way behind you: until the start of your next turn, no creature can enter the warp you came out of except you and those who came through with you.

features.name: Misplace
features.text:
As a Bonus Action, you can unravel one of your warps and choose a creature or an object you can see within 60 feet of yourself. An object can't be armor or clothing a creature is wearing or an object a creature is attuned to.
- **A creature** makes a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC; a willing creature can choose to fail. On a failed save, it is teleported into the space of another of your warps within 60 feet of yourself, or the nearest unoccupied space, and that warp's season, if any, takes it at once.
- **An object** that a creature is holding or carrying lets that creature make a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, the object appears in your hand or in the space of one of your warps. An object no one is holding or carrying gets no save.

features.name: Liminality
features.text: Iron and salt never stopped your Doors or Gates (see A Door of Your Own). From this level, other wards don't stop them either: your Gates and Doors work through effects that block teleportation or planar travel in a place (a ward, a circle, a hallowed or forbidden area), other than an *Antimagic Field*. An effect that stops a particular creature from teleporting (Cold Iron, Name It, the Iron Bell, a Hidden Killer's ward, a Faebreaker's grip) still stops that creature. Creatures that pass through your Gates and Doors don't trigger *Alarm*, *Glyph of Warding*, or similar warding magic, and need no invitation: an effect that keeps out uninvited creatures doesn't stop them. On foot, you're bound by such effects like anyone else (iron and salt at a door among them): the wall is your way in.

features.name: Outside
features.text: When an attack roll hits you or you fail a saving throw, you can take a Reaction and unravel one of your warps to step outside reality: the attack or effect does nothing to you. Until the start of your next turn, you can't be seen, targeted, or affected by anything, and you can't affect anything, though you keep Concentration. At the start of your next turn, you step back in, in the space you left or in an unoccupied space you can see within 30 feet of it. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclasses.name: Naming
subclasses.lead: You have learned the Names of all things, and you carve them into wood for control and consumption.

features.name: Naming Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Danae level specified in the Naming Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Danae Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Arcanist's Magic Aura*, *Identify*, *Illusory Script*, *Locate Object* |
| 5 | *Glyph of Warding*, *Tongues* |
| 7 | *Fire Shield*, *Locate Creature* |
| 9 | *Legend Lore*, *Scrying* |

features.name: Define
features.text:
Your Names are cut into staves of *feda*. As a Bonus Action, you define a creature, an object, or a place you can see within 60 feet of yourself, cutting its Name into a stave. Cutting a Name expends no warp, and a stave isn't one of your warps in place (you can't unravel it). A stave lasts until you finish a Long Rest or release it (no action required). You can keep a number of staves equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one); cutting another releases your oldest.

- **Named Creature.** You know its creature type, its Resistances, Immunities, and Vulnerabilities, and which of its saving throws has the lowest bonus. It can't hide from you, and the Invisible condition gives it no benefit against you. It also makes a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, it has Disadvantage on saving throws against your warps (Call included) while the stave lasts. On a successful save, the stave is still cut and you still learn what it tells you, but the creature has no Disadvantage against your warps, and you can't cut its Name again until you finish a Long Rest.
- **Named Object.** You can name only an object you have held, and only one object at a time; naming another releases the first. As a Bonus Action, you can summon it to your hand from anywhere on the same plane, unless another creature is holding or wearing it.
- **Named Place.** You always know the direction and distance to it.

*Ask the Name.* When you cut a Name, you can ask the DM one question about the thing you named, the kind of thing its Name would know: what it really is, who made it or owns it, where it has been, what was done there, what it wants. The DM answers truthfully, in a few words or a single image. You can ask a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest. You can ask about any one creature, object, or place only once per Long Rest. A Named creature that succeeds on its Charisma saving throw keeps its answer to itself.

features.name: Call
features.text: As a Bonus Action, you can speak the Name of a Named creature you can see, expending a warp. It makes a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC; a willing creature can choose to fail. On a failed save, it is teleported into the space of one of your warps within 60 feet of yourself, or the nearest unoccupied space.

features.name: Quick Cut
features.text: When you cut a Name, you can also make a warp as part of the same Bonus Action, expending a warp for it as usual.

features.name: Rename
features.text:
As a Magic action, you rename a Named creature, object, or place for 1 minute. It doesn't change: the renaming does only what the option you choose says, and nothing else about the thing is different. A creature, or an object a creature is holding or wearing, makes a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC to resist (the holder makes it for the object). Choose one:

- **Creature: Kind.** Effects that detect creatures by type, or that keep out, admit, or ward against creatures of a type (*Detect Evil and Good*, *Hallow*, *Magic Circle*, *Protection from Evil and Good*, a glyph or ward keyed to a type), treat it as a creature type of your choice. Nothing else does: damage, what a spell can target, and what an effect does once it applies all use its true type. Wards against the Hidden (iron and salt among them) answer to this too, though being Hidden isn't a creature type (see the box in the Introduction): you can also name a Hidden creature not Hidden, and it passes those wards as if it weren't, so you can walk yourself or a friend through a warded door.
- **Object: Purpose.** It is named another kind of object, and it serves only as that. Choose one: *Shut* (a door, gate, lid, or window named a wall can't be opened, short of breaking it); *Open* (a lock named open is unlocked); *Harmless* (a weapon or piece of ammunition named a feather deals no damage); or *Plain* (it looks, feels, and sounds like another nonmagical object of the same size or smaller, a cup named a crown, or a crown a cup, though *Detect Magic*, *Identify*, and The Sight see it as it is). A renamed object never gains magical properties, never counts as a Material component with a cost, and isn't treasure.
- **Place: Threshold.** A space up to a 10-foot Cube is named a threshold to the Hidden, which The Sight can see and Thresholds can open. This renaming lasts 10 minutes instead of 1.
- **Place: Home.** A space up to a 30-foot Cube is named your home. A creature you haven't invited can't willingly enter it.

Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.

features.name: Lasting Staves
features.text: Your staves no longer end when you finish a Long Rest; they last until you release them. A kept stave keeps its Named creature's Disadvantage against your warps with it.

features.name: Unmake
features.text: As a Magic action, you burn the stave of a Named creature you can see within 60 feet of yourself. It makes a Charisma saving throw against your spell save DC. On a failed save, for 1 minute the world forgets what it is: it loses all its Resistances and Immunities, including Immunities to conditions; effects that rely on its creature type don't apply to it; and it takes 4d10 Fire damage at the start of each of its turns as its Name burns. It repeats the save at the end of each of its turns, ending the effect on itself on a success. On a successful save, it takes 4d10 Fire damage once. The stave is consumed either way. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

subclasses.name: Shaping
subclasses.lead: You see the true shape of reality and alter it to your whims.

features.name: Shaping Spells
features.text:
When you reach a Danae level specified in the Shaping Spells table, you thereafter always have the listed spells prepared.

| Danae Level | Spells |
|---|---|
| 3 | *Floating Disk*, *Ice Knife*, *Levitate*, *Shatter* |
| 5 | *Meld into Stone*, *Tiny Hut* |
| 7 | *Fabricate*, *Stoneskin* |
| 9 | *Animate Objects*, *Creation* |

features.name: Stones
features.text: Your warps can be stones. A stone turns its Cube into solid ground, a wall (Total Cover), or a bridge, or opens a 5-foot-deep pit beneath its space. It is real, not an illusion; it has AC 15 and 30 Hit Points per 5-foot Cube. You can't make a stone on a creature (except a pillar or a pit, once you have Deep Ground at level 6), or make one that would leave a creature with no unoccupied space it could reach. Anything precious made this way is fairy gold (see Fae Weaving) and can't be made permanent.

features.name: Quick Weaving
features.text: As a Bonus Action, you can expend a warp to weave one object as Fae Weaving describes, without waiting for a rest and even before you have that feature. It lasts for 1 minute.

features.name: Deep Ground
features.text:
Your stones gain two shapes, a ramp or stair and a pillar that rises under a creature, lifting it 10 feet (when the stone ends, the pillar sinks back, lowering anything on it to the ground), and your pit can now open beneath a creature, which falls into the 5-foot-deep pit and has the Prone condition (when the stone ends, the ground rises back, lifting anything in the pit to the surface). A pillar or a pit can be made on a creature, following Warps' rule for that: the creature is lifted or falls only if it fails the Dexterity saving throw. Each stone takes only one shape.

With 1 hour of work, you can make a stone permanent; it no longer counts as a warp, so the warp it used comes back when you next finish a Short or Long Rest. You can have a number of permanent stones equal to your Charisma modifier (minimum of one); making another ends your oldest.

features.name: Dream Made Real
features.text: When you cast an illusion spell of level 1 or higher, you can make one object or surface in it real for as long as the illusion lasts. It must be Large or smaller and nonmagical, it can't deal damage, and it can't be made in a creature's space or enclose one. It is solid, bears weight, and blocks movement, and it is fairy gold. It can be a working thing, and it works as the real thing would: a rowboat that floats, a cart that rolls, a ladder with its winch, a locked door with its key.

features.name: Quarry
features.text: As a Magic action, you can place up to twelve 10-foot-Cube stones at once within 60 feet of yourself, in any shapes you know, ignoring the once-per-turn limit on making warps on creatures. They don't expend warps, and they last 1 hour; with 8 hours of work, the whole shape can be made permanent, and it counts as one of your permanent stones. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Long Rest.

multiclass.gains: Hit Point Die and training with Light armor
multiclass.text: You must have a Charisma score of 13 or higher. Gain the following traits from the Core Danae Traits table: Hit Point Die and training with Light armor. Gain the Danae's level 1 features, which are listed in the Danae Features table, except The Sight's skill proficiencies. For multiclass spell slots, add all your Danae levels, as you would Wizard levels. If you have levels in another class, you regain expended warps only when you finish a Long Rest.
